    **CI does NOT gate `cargo test` or `cargo clippy`** — never assume "CI green" means tests pass. The only CI code review is the Codex full-repo-review action (best-effort LLM pass, not a deterministic check).
    
    ## Conventional commits
    
    `feat` / `fix` / `docs` / etc. with scoped `(<crate>)` and `!` for breaking changes (e.g., `feat(op-plugins)!:`, `fix(mcp):`). Convention only — no enforced hook.
    
    ## Verify before marking done
    
    Run `/verify` before reporting work complete. CI won't catch fmt drift, clippy warnings, or test regressions, so the agent must. `/verify` runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`.
    
    ## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants (read these before touching plugins, state, or identity)
    
    - **Identity storage lifecycle (owner correction 2026-10-05).** Cozo owns identity-to-leaf/loop assignment and isolation. One immutable physical seed is shared through read-only views; each identity keeps its own writable leaf and the existing seven subvolumes. Only the external host provisioner may add a new blank leaf once, during explicit creation. Login, start, stop, logout, restart, bridge recovery and failed-start cleanup must NEVER add/remove Btrfs members. Start verifies/remounts the existing pair through the host mount owner; stop leaves membership and data intact. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage and records logical attachment. Do not interpret `attached=false` as device removal. No root copies, snapshots, new subvolumes or OverlayFS fallback during identity provisioning. Never modify a seed while retained leaves depend on it. Older add-on-start/remove-on-stop guidance in source, handoffs and signals is superseded; do not restore it. Host release snapshot/send/receive below is a separate deployment mechanism.
    - **D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`. No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops in plugin/service code. New backend capabilities register as plugins in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs` — never as new gRPC proto service packages.
    - **The plugin IS the schema — one source of truth, nonnegotiable.** That single schema is sealed into the blob, which IS the plugin. D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from it. Validate inputs against it. Each plugin defines its schema under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, using `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`. **There must be no parallel plugin schema source in a repository-level or plugin `schemas/` directory.** The former plugin capture directories, separate section files, and JSON-file loader have been removed. `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_loader.rs` still exists by name, but it reads only a manifest-pinned `PluginSchema` from the sealed blob catalog; it is not a file-schema fallback. The tched_router upstream document is imported once into `tched_router_contract.rs`; `tched_router_config_surface.rs` and its methods derive from that plugin-owned contract. Importing a new binary schema must replace that embedded contract through `gen_tched_router_config_surface --import-json`; it must not create a second captured-schema authority. Older docs claiming a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` are also stale — that file does not exist. Owner reaffirmed this rule on 2026-09-13.
    - **The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`. A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob`. Consumers read SHM directly (zero-copy) — they never re-hash and never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder and `live-schema.json` are gone.
    - **MutationEngine owns state; streaming comes from SHM (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** MutationEngine folds authoritative backend results into the complete state tree, including child objects, and commits that state to canonical SHM before change notifications. Child updates/deletions must preserve unrelated children and parent fields. Existing subscriptions derive their values from committed SHM; an in-memory event payload, method argument, or generator buffer is not a second state authority. Preserve verified principal/session scope for private state. Do not add a separate per-method streaming control plane or claim a buffered unary response provides state streaming.
    - **MCP gateway (settled).** One public MCP door: `:8090` on `op-grpc-bridge` (cognitive MCP is in-process there; no standalone `op-cognitive-mcp` runit service). `compact_mcp` is a retired plugin id. Compact *mode* (4 meta-tools) is in-process in op-web for the singleton control-plane chatbot; it is not an MCP plugin and not a second listener. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.
    - **External binaries back plugins; the plugin remains the single schema source.** 3tched-router / tched-router (`tched_router` in code) is the framework/schema/plugin integration backed by the autonomous `/usr/bin/zeroclaw` executable. The reproducible native input is pinned in `vendor/tched-router/source.pin`; `vendor/tched-router/build-native.sh` applies the checked-in patches and emits `target/native-artifacts/tched-router/{zeroclaw,manifest.json}` without installing it. `build-golden.sh` validates the pin, patch and binary provenance, then stages the binary, manifest, `/etc/op-dbus/zeroclaw-runtime.toml`, and the tracked default skill bundle into the golden filesystem. The `tched-router` runit service verifies that manifest, exact commit, binary digest, and version before exec, then seeds its private runtime config and skills from those staged bootstrap files. A fresh checkout includes the digest-pinned upstream source archive, patches and build recipe; the helper verifies and uses that archive by default. Cargo registry dependencies and system build tools still need provisioning. The executable keeps its upstream name. The plugin contract remains `tched_router_contract.rs`, and source attribution may identify `zeroclaw config schema`.
    - **Owner-confirmed lifecycle and model roles (2026-09-13, reaffirmed 2026-09-14).** Waypipe is retired: its crate directory, Cargo membership, binary target and protocol are absent; `retired-binaries`/`retired-services` prevent stale build or service artifacts from entering golden. Do not restore it in source exports or release inputs. Assistant is the control-plane chatbot, not an `assistant` container. The historical Gemma routing role is model agnostic; the `op-gemma` crate is retired (2026-09-19: directory, Cargo membership and binary removed, listed in `retired-binaries`) — the `gemma_brain` plugin remains and its role does not constrain the model/provider. Cargo membership and legacy names do not establish active deployments.
    - **Factory role correction (2026-09-14).** The former Factory account/platform plugin is retired from the registry and dispatch. The intended access is CLI/SSH; routing belongs to `tched_router`, and Factory billing requires an actual native binding. Provider names or relabelled direct upstream routes do not prove that binding. A future Missions integration needs its own verified native contract; do not restore the retired REST platform methods from historical fixtures or docs.
    - **Standalone vendor adapters are retired (2026-09-14).** The `op-grpc-adapters` crate directory and its `op.adapters.v1` protocol are absent after Netmaker retirement. Its duplicate mail/MQ services bypassed canonical plugin admission. Do not restore this crate or its old Netmaker clients. The existing bridge `operation.mail.v1` service and retained EMQX plugin are separate surfaces; their presence does not prove every mail or MQTT method is implemented.
    - **Owner-confirmed network topology (2026-09-13).** There is no WireGuard on this server. WireGuard terminates at the decoy; identity is transported by WARP. WireGuard types, plugin declarations, credentials or historical configuration paths in source do not establish a server WireGuard interface or a requirement to install one. Classify those surfaces by their decoy/server role before proposing implementation or retirement. An unwired `wgcf` method is not evidence that the actual WARP identity transport is broken.
    - **Identity minting and metadata (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** The identity subsystem owns minting the identity and its SealedId/SID1 credential blob. This is distinct from an OPBLOB01 plugin blob and does not belong in the plugin catalog. Clients forward the authored credential through the transport's identity metadata; they do not mint or reconstruct it from genesis/trace/key headers. Verify minting, persistence, injection and receiver validation as separate links. Current source assigns session/SID1 creation to MutationEngine with the op-identity format; the existence of an HTTP/MCP helper does not prove every gRPC client injects SID1.
    - **Owner decisions: decoy GRE, TLS and identity injection (2026-09-25).** The owner directed these changes; do not restore the previous layout. The door stays `10.0.0.2:8090`: tonic with the internal `svc0` certificate from the op-dbus local CA. The bridge no longer listens on `127.0.0.1:8090` or `10.0.0.3:8090`, and it no longer serves a second browser certificate. Browser-facing TLS terminates on the decoy at `10.0.0.1`. The decoy mints the sealed identity blob, and WARP delivers it to the 8090 interceptor, which anchors the session and writes the identity metadata (`anchor_verified_human_session` and `insert_identity_metadata` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs`). The oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed proof of the WireGuard peer, because WireGuard exists only on the decoy; the human credential (SID1) is the session identity for that key. The bridge's own client and MutationEngine are the wrong place for session or identity injection. Source and live state do not match this yet (2026-09-25): the interceptor still mints genesis server-side when no session exists (`mint_and_store_genesis` in `anchor_verified_human_session`), the decoy issuer mints only OIA1, and the decoy routes browser traffic for `10.0.0.2` over `gre-host` with no WARP route in either main routing table. The `gre-decoy` tunnel joins decoy and host (`deploy/runit/gre-decoy`): outer `188.68.58.237` ↔ `129.80.64.127`, inner `192.168.255.1/30` plus `10.0.0.2/32`, with `10.0.0.1` and the WireGuard clients `10.0.0.5`–`10.0.0.7` routed via `192.168.255.2`. GRE routing replaces NAT on this path: nftables is the firewall only, never a router, so do not add DNAT, SNAT or masquerade for it. Filter rules such as accepting GRE from the decoy are fine. GRE is not encrypted, so anything crossing it that is not TLS is readable on the path. MQTT stays on `10.0.0.3`, aliased on `ovsbr0` beside the OpenFlow address `10.200.0.1`. Xray runs in its container. op-web's page address is `http://10.0.0.4:8080`: plain HTTP outside the TLS zone, with `10.0.0.4/32` on `gre-decoy` and routed from the decoy over `gre-host`. The decoy issuer (`/etc/systemd/system/op-decoy-issuer.service.d/browser-auth.conf` on the decoy, not in this repo) hands out the IP door `https://10.0.0.2:8090` and allows the `10.0.0.4` and `10.0.0.2` page origins; no domain name points browsers at the decoy. Still open on 2026-09-25: how the decoy-minted oracle reaches the interceptor. The owner's direction is that it travels over GRE; whether it rides inside the relayed request or separately is undecided. Until that lands, the deployed page still fetches OIA1 from `http://10.0.0.1:51888/identity/self`, and the door rejects a request that carries no credential.
    - **Btrfs storage and transport (owner correction 2026-09-23).** Deployment remains the prepared snapshot transferred by `btrfs send/receive`. The earlier global five-subvolume limit and instruction to replace Snowball/cache subvolumes with ordinary directories are withdrawn. Preserve the original `operation-dbus-proto` cache/NUMA/timing architecture: Btrfs cache category subvolumes; authoritative timing plus vector/state subvolumes; aligned read-only snapshot sets and send/receive. See the original repo `branding/product-baseline.md` §12 and `crates/op-snowball/{DESIGN,REQUIREMENTS}.md` (R5). Retention is configurable per storage owner, not a global five-subvolume cap. Parent snapshots do not include nested subvolume contents: snapshot and transport every required member explicitly. Never flatten existing subvolumes or delete historical data to satisfy the withdrawn limit. Preserve security, writer-locking, identity and error-handling fixes while correcting storage regressions.
    - **No SQLite — use CozoDB.** CozoDB (`op-cozo-store`) is the embedded database for this project. Do not add new `rusqlite` or other SQLite use. `op-cache/src/btrfs_cache.rs` already uses a Cozo index; current `workstack_cache.rs`, `workflow_cache.rs`, `workflow_tracker.rs`, and `pattern_tracker.rs` still use `rusqlite` and remain migration debt rather than an approved pattern.
    - **RAG pipeline and Voyage-4 models.** Live source file indexing goes through `code_index` (mode='source') into Qdrant collections: `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_large` and `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_lite`. Voyage-4 models are interchangeable across their dimension (1024 for all variants); `_large` and `_lite` refer to model size/quality tier, not embedding space. All collections share a single fused retrieval space and can be queried together. Legacy `repos_lsp_*_voyage_code_4` collections and `repomix_rag` collection are retired — do not use them. NotebookLM integration is removed.
    
    ## Handoff between agents
    
    Claude, Codex, Grok and any other agent share one handoff: `HANDOFF.md`. Read it
    at the start of every session, after this file. Claim your task in its *Active
    work* table before changing anything, and never reset, stash or overwrite work
    another agent has claimed there. Before the session ends, or before a context or
    usage limit, update your row and add a dated *Handoff* entry. A handoff kept only
    in one agent's private memory is invisible to the others, so it does not count.
    
    ## Signals and task board
    
    - **Append observations to `SIGNALS.md`** rather than letting them evaporate in chat. Three signal types: `💡 SUGGESTION` · `⚠️ CONCERN` · `👁️ OBSERVATION`. Each row: date · model · signal · optional `→ OD-##` link. Models leave status `open`. Promote anything actionable to `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.
    - **`WISHLIST.md` is the canonical task board** — do not create new TODO docs. Priority buckets: Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff. Dispatch syntax: "dispatch <ID> to <agent>" spawns an agent with the task context and updates status here.
    - **Read recent `SIGNALS.md` rows before non-trivial work** in the area they touch — the file records load-bearing gotchas (stale vendored deps, live/deployed drift, the live-vs-intent identity topology) that source alone will not surface.
    
    ## Stale documentation
    
    - **README.md is stale**: crate count (31) is wrong, `cd lovable` is a deleted directory, `sudo service6` references are retired. Prefer AGENTS.md and source over README claims.
    - Many older deploy scripts and HANDOFF docs still reference s6 — treat them as archival; runit/`sv` is current.
    - Anything mentioning `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`, `live-schema.json`, or `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` is describing a retired design.
    - Anything mentioning `OIB1`, `oib1:`, `blob_ref`, `SessionIdentityBlob`, or `x-opdbus-identity-blob-bin` is pre-2026-09-01 and stale; the session-identity envelope is now `SID1` / `SealedId`.
    - Anything referencing `crates/op-web/ui/`, `zeroclaw-gui`, pairing codes, or `operation-dashboard-ui-07` — the production UI is `/srv/git/3tched.com` (github.com/repr0bated/3tched.com), deployed from that repo through `scripts/publish-op-web.sh`. `LANDING` selects the mount name; `URL_PREFIX=/` selects the dashboard root.
    - Older deployment-script and backup/restore hierarchy descriptions are not current deployment authority. Deployment is btrfs send/receive of the prepared snapshot — see architecture invariants above.
    
    ## Subagent and model selection
    
    **Owner preference (2026-09-13, model names withdrawn 2026-09-24,
    reaffirmed 2026-09-30): assess task
    difficulty and required reasoning before delegation, and use the cheapest
    available model that can complete it at the same quality.** A lower price must
    not thin the answer, skip evidence, or weaken a judgment. If the cheaper model
    would lose accuracy, completeness, or care, use the more capable model. Pick
    from the models the session can actually launch. Do not inherit an expensive
    parent model by default, and do not pin a product or model id in this file.
    Use a low-cost model for lookups, inventory extraction, documentation
    assembly, builds, tests, and routine checks when that model can match the
    quality of a more capable one. Choose low effort for mechanical work and
    medium effort for bounded reasoning. Escalate when the task's quality needs
    it or a cheaper attempt falls short, and briefly state why.
    
    Keep the primary agent available for user communication and coordination.
    Delegate longer execution and research jobs, use nonblocking progress checks,
    and avoid long blocking tool calls on the primary. User messages steer active
    work; answer them promptly while delegated work continues. Small immediate
    edits and decisions can remain with the primary when delegation would add
    overhead.
    
    Prefer the **least-expensive subagent whose output matches a more capable model** for builds and tests:
    
    - `Explore` (fast read-only) for locating code, grepping symbols, answering "where is X."
    - `Plan` for architecture and design before writing code.
    - `general-purpose` only when the task needs multi-step reasoning or execution that Explore or Plan cannot cover.
    - Use a more capable model for complex cross-crate reasoning, security review, or ambiguous architectural decisions, and for any standard edit, build fix, or test whose quality would drop on the low-cost agent.
    - Do not spawn a subagent for a single-file edit or a direct grep you can do yourself.

    ### 2026-10-02T20:35Z · Haiku (OD-98: proper atomic migration helper added)
    
    The simple `update-chatbot-fsid` utility failed because identity records require **atomic intent transactions** (the system enforces safety).
    
    Created proper migration helper: **`migrate-chatbot-root`**
    
    This new utility guides through the official three-step atomic migration procedure from the receipt:
    
    1. **preflight**: Get current state via `inspect_own_physical_root_migration_preflight`
       - Requires authenticated D-Bus access (lungs.sock or SID1)
       - Returns safe metadata for plan construction
    
    2. **prepare**: Create migration plan JSON with all required fields
       - Plan location: `/var/lib/op-dbus/identity-physical-migration-plans/b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28.json`
       - Compute SHA256 of plan file
       - Includes seed FSID, leaf info, native root, Incus instance JSON
    
    3. **migrate**: Call `migrate_own_physical_root` with plan SHA256
       - Atomic transaction preserves credentials, SID1, genesis, actor class
       - Archives old bindings, records new physical provenance
       - Advances revision atomically
       - No ADD_DEV/RM_DEV, only verification
    
    Usage:
    ```bash
    cargo run --bin migrate-chatbot-root -p op-cozo-store -- preflight
    cargo run --bin migrate-chatbot-root -p op-cozo-store -- prepare
    cargo run --bin migrate-chatbot-root -p op-cozo-store -- migrate
    ```
    
    This is a root-owned operation following the procedure in `reports/identity-replacement/20260930/cozo-reconciliation/receipt.md`.

    # Cargo worker routing
    
    The ordinary `cargo` command delegates to a worker:
    
    | Caller | Runner | Model |
    |---|---|---|
    | GPT / Codex | Codex CLI | `gpt-6-luna` |
    | Grok | Cursor Agent | `composer-2.5` |
    | Claude | Claude CLI | `haiku` |
    
    Set `CARGO_CALLER_FAMILY=gpt`, `grok`, or `claude` in the calling agent's environment. This explicit setting takes precedence over optional `CARGO_CALLER_MODEL`, `CURSOR_MODEL`, `GROK_MODEL` and Claude/Grok environment hints. Unmarked shells use GPT/Luna. These hints select a worker; they do not establish an authenticated identity. Cursor does not expose a verified caller-model marker, so select the family explicitly when switching models there.
    
    `source scripts/cargo-aliases.bash` installs an exported Bash `cargo` function. The user PATH shim also covers shells that do not expand aliases. Normal syntax is unchanged: `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo metadata`, and so on. Commands in this workspace run from its repository root.
    
    The worker executes one fixed helper with the original argument array. Native Cargo stdout, stderr and exit status return to the caller; model commentary does not pollute JSON output. Requests use private temporary files and a per-workspace dispatch lock. A missing runner or completion receipt fails without executing Cargo locally. `CARGO_DISPATCHED=1` is the worker recursion guard; native Cargo remains at `/usr/bin/cargo`.
    
    Model/runner overrides are `CARGO_MODEL_GPT`, `CARGO_MODEL_GROK`, `CARGO_MODEL_CLAUDE` and the corresponding `CARGO_RUNNER_*` variables. `CARGO_DISPATCH_DRY_RUN=1 cargo check` prints the routing plan without invoking a model or Cargo. No permission-bypass flags are supplied to the runners.
    
    `bash scripts/tests/test-cargo-dispatch.sh` checks all routes, exact argument handling, output/status propagation, missing completion and recursion with fake runners. It never invokes real Cargo or a model. On 2026-10-03 all three actual runners completed `cargo --version` and returned the native version output. This verifies model access and execution routing; it is not a full build validation.

        pub fn lungs(

            if let Lungs::Socket { session, .. } = &lungs
                && !session.is_empty()

            };

                namespace,
                open_files: HashMap::new(),
                next_fh: 1,
                uid: unsafe { libc::getuid() },
                gid: unsafe { libc::getgid() },

                .get(&(plugin_id.to_string(), method.to_string()))
                .map(|outcome| {
                    if error {
                        outcome.error.clone()
                    } else {
                        outcome.result.clone()
                    }
                })
                .unwrap_or_default()
        }
    
        /// Run one lungs call and record its receipt or diagnostic. The errno
        /// tells the writer which stage failed; the `error` file says why.
        fn lungs_call(
            &mut self,
            plugin_id: &str,
            method: &str,
            bytes: &[u8],
        ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, (i32, Vec<u8>)> {
            let outcome = self.run_lungs_call(plugin_id, method, bytes);
            let entry = self
                .outcomes
                .entry((plugin_id.to_string(), method.to_string()))
                .or_default();
            match outcome {
                Ok(receipt) => {
                    entry.result = pretty(&receipt);
                    entry.error.clear();
                    Ok(entry.result.clone())
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    entry.result.clear();
                    entry.error = pretty(&serde_json::json!({
                        "plugin": plugin_id,
                        "method": method,
                        "stage": error.stage(),
                        "error": error.to_string(),
                    }));
                    Err((error.errno(), entry.error.clone()))
                }
            }
        }

                .lungs
                .as_ref()
                .ok_or_else(|| LungsError::Transport("not a lungs mount".into()))?;
            let arguments: Value =

                dispatch::method_decl(&self.store, &self.namespace.target, plugin_id, method_name)
                    .map_err(|error| LungsError::Arguments(error.to_string()))?;

                Lungs::Socket { .. } => None,
                Lungs::Credential { credential, .. } => Some(dispatch::read_credential(credential)?),

            // block on another future. A scoped thread with its own runtime keeps
            // the D-Bus round trip off that context.

                            .enable_all()

                            match (lungs, credential) {
                                (Lungs::Credential { bus_address, .. }, Some(credential)) => {
                                    dispatch::call_as_identity(

                                        plugin_id,
                                        method_name,

        pub fn validate_value(&self, root: &Value, base: Option<&Value>) -> Result<()> {

            for (name, field) in &self.fields {

                        .validate(value, root)

                    None if field.required => bail!("required field /{name} is missing"),
                    None => {}
                }
            }
    
            if let Some(base) = base {
                let base_object = base
                    .as_object()
                    .with_context(|| format!("base {} state must be an object", self.name))?;

    const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b"OPBLOB01";
    const HEADER_LEN: usize = 64;
    const SECTION_ENTRY_LEN: usize = 24;
    const SECTION_SCHEMA_JSON: u32 = 1;
    
    pub const DEFAULT_CATALOG_DIR: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs";
    pub const DEFAULT_STATE_DIR: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/state";

            Self {
                catalog_dir: catalog_dir.into(),
                state_dir: state_dir.into(),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn capture(&self) -> Result<SourceSnapshot> {
            for _ in 0..4 {
                let catalog_before = self.read_catalog_manifest()?;
                let state_before = self.read_state_generation()?;
                let mut objects = BTreeMap::new();
    
                for (plugin_id, schema_hash) in &catalog_before.plugins {
                    let schema = self.read_schema(plugin_id, schema_hash)?;
                    let value = self.read_state(plugin_id, &schema);
                    let object =
                        TypedObjectBlob::new(plugin_id.clone(), schema_hash.clone(), schema, value)
                            .with_context(|| format!("validate typed source object '{plugin_id}'"))?;
                    objects.insert(plugin_id.clone(), object);
                }
    
                let catalog_after = self.read_catalog_manifest()?;
                let state_after = self.read_state_generation()?;
                if catalog_before == catalog_after && state_before == state_after {
                    return Ok(SourceSnapshot {
                        catalog_hash: catalog_after.catalog_hash,
                        catalog_generation: catalog_after.generation,
                        objects,
                    });
                }
            }
    
            bail!("SHM source changed during four capture attempts")
        }
    
        fn read_catalog_manifest(&self) -> Result<CatalogManifest> {
            read_json(self.catalog_dir.join(".manifest.json"))
        }
    
        fn read_state_generation(&self) -> Result<u64> {
            let path = self.state_dir.join(".manifest.json");
            if !path.exists() {
                return Ok(0);
            }
            Ok(read_json::<StateManifest>(path)?.generation)
        }

        /// Falls back to schema-derived defaults when the file is missing,
        /// unreadable, or does not validate against the sealed schema.
        fn read_state(&self, plugin_id: &str, schema: &PluginSchema) -> serde_json::Value {
            let path = self.state_dir.join(format!("{plugin_id}.json"));
            match fs::read(&path) {
                Ok(bytes) => match serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&bytes) {
                    Ok(value) => match schema.validate_value(&value, None) {
                        Ok(()) => value,
                        Err(e) => {
                            if std::env::var("THREETCHEDFS_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                                eprintln!("3tchedfs: state fallback for {plugin_id}: {e}");
                            }
                            schema.template()
                        }
                    },
                    Err(e) => {
                        if std::env::var("THREETCHEDFS_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                            eprintln!("3tchedfs: state parse error for {plugin_id}: {e}");
                        }
                        schema.template()
                    }
                },
                Err(e) => {
                    if std::env::var("THREETCHEDFS_DEBUG").is_ok() {
                        eprintln!("3tchedfs: state read error for {plugin_id}: {e}");
                    }
                    schema.template()
                }
            }
        }
    
        fn read_schema(&self, plugin_id: &str, expected_hash: &str) -> Result<PluginSchema> {
            if plugin_id.is_empty()
                || plugin_id.len() > 128
                || !plugin_id
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_lowercase() || byte.is_ascii_digit() || byte == b'_')
            {
                bail!("invalid canonical plugin id '{plugin_id}'");
            }
            if expected_hash.len() != 64
                || !expected_hash
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&byte))
            {
                bail!("invalid schema hash for '{plugin_id}'");
            }
            let file = self
                .catalog_dir
                .join(format!("{plugin_id}.{}.blob", &expected_hash[..16]));
            let bytes =
                fs::read(&file).with_context(|| format!("read source blob {}", file.display()))?;
            let blob = OpBlobRef::new(&bytes)
                .with_context(|| format!("decode source blob {}", file.display()))?;
            let actual_hash = blob.schema_hash_hex();
            if actual_hash != expected_hash {
                bail!(
                    "manifest hash mismatch for '{plugin_id}': expected {expected_hash}, got {actual_hash}"
                );
            }
            // The schema's own authority decodes it, so this projection reads
            // exactly what was sealed; `from_sealed` then fails to compile, not to
            // capture, whenever the authority's shape changes.
            let sealed: op_state_store::PluginSchema = serde_json::from_slice(blob.schema_json())
                .with_context(|| format!("decode sealed PluginSchema for '{plugin_id}'"))?;
            crate::model::from_sealed(sealed)
                .with_context(|| format!("convert sealed PluginSchema for '{plugin_id}'"))
        }
    }
    
    struct OpBlobRef<'a> {
        bytes: &'a [u8],
        schema_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
    }
    
    impl<'a> OpBlobRef<'a> {
        fn new(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self> {
            if bytes.len() < HEADER_LEN || &bytes[..8] != MAGIC {
                bail!("not an OPBLOB01 blob");
            }
            let version = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[8], bytes[9]]);
            if version != 1 {
                bail!("unsupported OPBLOB format version {version}");
            }
            let count = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[10], bytes[11]]) as usize;
            let table_end = HEADER_LEN
                .checked_add(
                    count
                        .checked_mul(SECTION_ENTRY_LEN)
                        .context("section count overflow")?,
                )
                .context("section table overflow")?;
            if table_end > bytes.len() {
                bail!("section table overruns blob");
            }
    
            let mut schema_range = None;
            for index in 0..count {
                let entry = HEADER_LEN + index * SECTION_ENTRY_LEN;
                let tag = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[entry..entry + 4].try_into()?);
                let offset = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[entry + 8..entry + 16].try_into()?) as usize;
                let length = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[entry + 16..entry + 24].try_into()?) as usize;
                let end = offset
                    .checked_add(length)
                    .context("section range overflow")?;
                if end > bytes.len() {
                    bail!("section {tag} overruns blob");
                }
                if tag == SECTION_SCHEMA_JSON && schema_range.replace(offset..end).is_some() {
                    bail!("duplicate schema section");
                }
            }
    
            let schema_range = schema_range.context("missing schema section")?;
            let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
            hasher.update(&bytes[schema_range.clone()]);
            if hasher.finalize().as_slice() != &bytes[16..48] {
                bail!("schema hash mismatch: blob is corrupt or tampered");
            }
    
            Ok(Self {
                bytes,
                schema_range,
            })
        }
    
        fn schema_json(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
            &self.bytes[self.schema_range.clone()]
        }
    
        fn schema_hash_hex(&self) -> String {
            self.bytes[16..48]
                .iter()
                .map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}"))
                .collect()
        }
    }
    
    fn read_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<T> {
        let path = path.as_ref();
        let bytes = fs::read(path).with_context(|| format!("read {}", path.display()))?;
        serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).with_context(|| format!("decode {}", path.display()))
    }

    pub const ROOT_INO: u64 = 1;
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub enum ProjectionTarget {
        View(String),
        Workspace(String),
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct Namespace {
        pub nodes: HashMap<u64, Node>,
        pub children: HashMap<u64, BTreeMap<OsString, u64>>,
        pub target: ProjectionTarget,
        /// SHM state directory for live reads (`/dev/shm/opdbus/state`).
        /// Only used for view mounts; workspace mounts use frozen COW objects.
        pub state_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
        /// Lungs mounts belong to one identity and expose a `call` file per
        /// method, so a write is that identity's canonical call.
        pub lungs: bool,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct Node {
        pub ino: u64,
        pub parent: u64,
        pub name: OsString,
        pub path: String,
        pub kind: NodeKind,
        pub write_target: Option<WriteTarget>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub enum NodeKind {
        Directory,
        File(Arc<RwLock<Vec<u8>>>),
        /// A file whose content is read live from the SHM state tree at open time.
        /// Only used for read-only view mounts. `plugin_id` is a catalog-known
        /// name (validated during capture); `pointer` is a JSON pointer into the
        /// plugin's state object. `schema` is pinned from the sealed blob.
        LiveFile {
            plugin_id: String,
            pointer: String,
        },
        Symlink(String),
        /// Lungs control file. A complete JSON write, flushed on close, is
        /// validated against the sealed method schema and dispatched as the
        /// mount's identity. Nothing is stored in the file itself.
        CallFile {
            plugin_id: String,
            method: String,
        },
        /// The last receipt (`error: false`) or diagnostic (`error: true`) of the
        /// lungs call for `plugin_id.method`.
        Outcome {
            plugin_id: String,
            method: String,
            error: bool,
        },
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct WriteTarget {
        pub workspace_id: String,
        pub plugin_id: String,
        pub pointer: String,
    }
    
    impl Namespace {
        pub fn build(
            store: &ObjectStore,
            target: ProjectionTarget,
            state_dir: Option<&std::path::Path>,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            Self::build_with(store, target, state_dir, false)
        }
    
        /// A live view for one identity, with a lungs `call` file per method.
        pub fn build_lungs(
            store: &ObjectStore,
            target: ProjectionTarget,
            state_dir: &std::path::Path,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            if !matches!(target, ProjectionTarget::View(_)) {
                bail!("a lungs mount projects a pinned view, not a workspace");
            }
            Self::build_with(store, target, Some(state_dir), true)
        }
    
        pub fn build_with(
            store: &ObjectStore,
            target: ProjectionTarget,
            state_dir: Option<&std::path::Path>,
            lungs: bool,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            let (view, workspace) = match &target {
                ProjectionTarget::View(id) => (store.read_view(id)?, None),
                ProjectionTarget::Workspace(id) => {
                    let workspace = store.read_workspace(id)?;
                    let view = store.read_view(&workspace.base_view)?;
                    (view, Some(workspace))
                }
            };
            // View mounts read live state from SHM; workspace mounts use frozen COW.
            let live = workspace.is_none() && state_dir.is_some();
            let mut builder =
                NamespaceBuilder::new(target.clone(), state_dir.map(|p| p.to_path_buf()), lungs);
            builder.add_root_metadata(&view, workspace.as_ref())?;
    
            let plugins = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "plugins")?;
            let operations = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "operations")?;
            let relationships = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "relationships")?;
            let dependencies = builder.add_dir(relationships, "dependencies")?;
            let capabilities = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "capabilities")?;
    
            for plugin_id in view.objects.keys() {
                let object = match &workspace {
                    Some(workspace) => store.workspace_object(workspace, plugin_id)?,
                    None => store.object_for_view(&view, plugin_id)?,
                };
                let plugin_name = encode_component(plugin_id);
                let plugin_dir = builder.add_dir(plugins, &plugin_name)?;
                builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "object.blob.json", &object, None)?;
                builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "schema.json", &object.schema, None)?;
                if live {
                    builder.add_live_file(plugin_dir, "value.json", plugin_id, "")?;
                } else {
                    builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "value.json", &object.value, None)?;
                }
                builder.add_json(
                    plugin_dir,
                    "capabilities.json",
                    &object.schema.required_capabilities(),
                    None,
                )?;
                builder.add_text(
                    plugin_dir,
                    "object.hash",
                    format!(
                        "{}\n",
                        object_hash_for_target(&view, workspace.as_ref(), plugin_id)?
                    )
                    .into_bytes(),
                    None,
                )?;
    
                let data_dir = builder.add_dir(plugin_dir, "data")?;
                let workspace_id = workspace
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|workspace| workspace.workspace_id.clone());
                builder.add_value_children(
                    data_dir,
                    plugin_id,
                    "",
                    &object.value,
                    Some(&object.schema),
                    None,
                    workspace_id.as_deref(),
                    !object.schema.tags.iter().any(|tag| tag == "immutable"),
                    live,
                )?;
    
                let methods_dir = builder.add_dir(plugin_dir, "operations")?;
                let root_methods_dir = builder.add_dir(operations, &plugin_name)?;
                for (method_name, method) in &object.schema.methods {
                    let encoded = encode_component(method_name);
                    let method_dir = builder.add_dir(methods_dir, &encoded)?;
                    builder.add_json(method_dir, "input.schema.json", &method.args, None)?;
                    if let Some(returns) = &method.returns {
                        builder.add_json(method_dir, "output.schema.json", returns, None)?;
                    }
                    builder.add_json(method_dir, "metadata.json", method, None)?;
                    if lungs {
                        builder.add_lungs_files(method_dir, plugin_id, method_name)?;
                    }
                    builder.add_symlink(
                        root_methods_dir,
                        &encoded,
                        format!("/plugins/{plugin_name}/operations/{encoded}"),
                    )?;
    
                    if let Some(capability) = &method.required_capability {
                        let capability_dir =
                            builder.add_dir_idempotent(capabilities, &encode_component(capability))?;
                        builder.add_symlink(
                            capability_dir,
                            &format!("{plugin_name}.{}", encode_component(method_name)),
                            format!("/plugins/{plugin_name}/operations/{encoded}"),
                        )?;
                    }
                }
    
                let relation_dir = builder.add_dir(dependencies, &plugin_name)?;
                for dependency in &object.schema.dependencies {
                    builder.add_symlink(
                        relation_dir,
                        &encode_component(dependency),
                        format!("/plugins/{}", encode_component(dependency)),
                    )?;
                }
            }
    
            Ok(builder.finish())
        }
    
        pub fn node(&self, ino: u64) -> Option<&Node> {
            self.nodes.get(&ino)
        }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct ViewManifest {
        pub format: String,
        pub view_id: String,
        pub source_catalog_hash: String,
        pub source_catalog_generation: u64,
        pub parent_view: Option<String>,
        pub objects: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct ViewBody {
        format: String,
        source_catalog_hash: String,
        source_catalog_generation: u64,
        parent_view: Option<String>,
        objects: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct Workspace {
        pub format: String,
        pub workspace_id: String,
        pub base_view: String,
        pub staged_objects: BTreeMap<String, String>,
        pub committed_view: Option<String>,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct ObjectStore {
        root: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl ObjectStore {
        pub fn open(root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Result<Self> {
            let store = Self { root: root.into() };
            for directory in [
                store.objects_dir(),
                store.views_dir(),
                store.workspaces_dir(),
                store.snapshots_dir(),
            ] {
                fs::create_dir_all(&directory)
                    .with_context(|| format!("create store directory {}", directory.display()))?;
            }
            Ok(store)
        }
    
        pub fn capture(&self, source: &SourceCatalog, activate: bool) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            let snapshot = source.capture()?;
            self.capture_snapshot(snapshot, activate)
        }
    
        pub fn capture_snapshot(
            &self,
            snapshot: SourceSnapshot,
            activate: bool,
        ) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            let mut objects = BTreeMap::new();
            for (plugin_id, object) in snapshot.objects {
                let hash = self.write_object(&object)?;
                objects.insert(plugin_id, hash);
            }
    
            if let Some(current) = self.current_view().transpose()?
                && current.source_catalog_hash == snapshot.catalog_hash
                && current.source_catalog_generation == snapshot.catalog_generation
                && current.objects == objects
            {
                return Ok(current);
            }
    
            let parent_view = self.current_view_id()?;
            let body = ViewBody {
                format: FORMAT_VERSION.to_string(),
                source_catalog_hash: snapshot.catalog_hash,
                source_catalog_generation: snapshot.catalog_generation,
                parent_view,
                objects,
            };
            let view = self.write_view(body)?;
            if activate {
                self.set_current(&view.view_id)?;
            }
            Ok(view)
        }
    
        pub fn create_workspace(
            &self,
            workspace_id: Option<&str>,
            base_view: Option<&str>,
        ) -> Result<Workspace> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            let id = workspace_id
                .map(ToOwned::to_owned)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| Uuid::new_v4().to_string());
            validate_name(&id, "workspace")?;
            let base_view = match base_view {
                Some(id) => {
                    self.read_view(id)?;
                    id.to_string()
                }
                None => self
                    .current_view_id()?
                    .context("no current view; capture the SHM source first")?,
            };
            let workspace = Workspace {
                format: FORMAT_VERSION.to_string(),
                workspace_id: id.clone(),
                base_view,
                staged_objects: BTreeMap::new(),
                committed_view: None,
            };
            let path = self.workspace_path(&id);
            if path.exists() {
                bail!("workspace '{id}' already exists");
            }
            self.atomic_json(&path, &workspace)?;
            Ok(workspace)
        }
    
        pub fn read_workspace(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Workspace> {
            validate_name(id, "workspace")?;
            self.read_json(self.workspace_path(id))
        }
    
        fn stage_state_locked(
            &self,
            mut workspace: Workspace,
            plugin_id: &str,
            value: Value,
        ) -> Result<String> {
            if workspace.committed_view.is_some() {
                bail!(
                    "workspace '{}' is already committed",
                    workspace.workspace_id
                );
            }
            let current_object = self.workspace_object(&workspace, plugin_id)?;
            let base_view = self.read_view(&workspace.base_view)?;
            let immutable_base = self.object_for_view(&base_view, plugin_id)?;
            let object = TypedObjectBlob::new(
                plugin_id.to_string(),
                current_object.source_schema_hash.clone(),
                current_object.schema.clone(),
                value,
            )?;
            object.validate(Some(&immutable_base.value))?;
            let hash = self.write_object(&object)?;
            workspace
                .staged_objects
                .insert(plugin_id.to_string(), hash.clone());
            self.atomic_json(&self.workspace_path(&workspace.workspace_id), &workspace)?;
            Ok(hash)
        }
    
        pub fn stage_pointer(
            &self,
            workspace_id: &str,
            plugin_id: &str,
            pointer: &str,
            value: Value,
        ) -> Result<String> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            let workspace = self.read_workspace(workspace_id)?;
            let object = self.workspace_object(&workspace, plugin_id)?;
            let mut state = object.value;
            set_json_pointer(&mut state, pointer, value)?;
            self.stage_state_locked(workspace, plugin_id, state)
        }
    
        pub fn commit_workspace(&self, workspace_id: &str, activate: bool) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            let mut workspace = self.read_workspace(workspace_id)?;
            if let Some(view_id) = &workspace.committed_view {
                return self.read_view(view_id);
            }
            if activate && self.current_view_id()?.as_deref() != Some(workspace.base_view.as_str()) {
                bail!(
                    "workspace base {} is stale; current view changed",
                    workspace.base_view
                );
            }
            let base = self.read_view(&workspace.base_view)?;
            let mut objects = base.objects.clone();
            objects.extend(workspace.staged_objects.clone());
            let body = ViewBody {
                format: FORMAT_VERSION.to_string(),
                source_catalog_hash: base.source_catalog_hash,
                source_catalog_generation: base.source_catalog_generation,
                parent_view: Some(base.view_id.clone()),
                objects,
            };
            let view = self.write_view(body)?;
            if activate {
                self.set_current(&view.view_id)?;
            }
            workspace.committed_view = Some(view.view_id.clone());
            self.atomic_json(&self.workspace_path(workspace_id), &workspace)?;
            Ok(view)
        }
    
        pub fn abort_workspace(&self, workspace_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            let workspace = self.read_workspace(workspace_id)?;
            if workspace.committed_view.is_some() {
                bail!("workspace '{workspace_id}' is committed and cannot be aborted");
            }
            fs::remove_file(self.workspace_path(workspace_id))
                .with_context(|| format!("remove workspace '{workspace_id}'"))
        }
    
        pub fn snapshot(&self, name: &str, view_id: Option<&str>) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            let _lock = self.lock_exclusive()?;
            validate_name(name, "snapshot")?;
            let view = match view_id {
                Some(view_id) => self.read_view(view_id)?,
                None => self
                    .current_view()
                    .transpose()?
                    .context("no current view")?,
            };
            let path = self.snapshot_path(name);
            if path.exists() {
                bail!("snapshot '{name}' already exists");
            }
            self.atomic_write(&path, format!("{}\n", view.view_id).as_bytes())?;
            Ok(view)
        }
    
        pub fn read_snapshot(&self, name: &str) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            validate_name(name, "snapshot")?;
            let id = fs::read_to_string(self.snapshot_path(name))
                .with_context(|| format!("read snapshot '{name}'"))?;
            self.read_view(id.trim())
        }
    
        pub fn current_view_id(&self) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    fn pretty(value: &impl serde::Serialize) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(value).unwrap_or_default();
        bytes.push(b'\n');
        bytes
    }
    
    /// A workspace field or a lungs call file accepts writes; nothing else does.
    fn node_writable(node: &Node) -> bool {
        node.write_target.is_some() || matches!(node.kind, NodeKind::CallFile { .. })
    }
    
    impl Filesystem for TypedFuse {
        fn init(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, config: &mut KernelConfig) -> Result<(), i32> {
            // Typed files must be parsed and committed only after a complete
            // write. Ask the kernel to deliver O_TRUNC with open(), where a file
            // handle can buffer the replacement until flush/release.
            config
                .add_capabilities(fuser::consts::FUSE_ATOMIC_O_TRUNC)
                .map_err(|_| EIO)?;
            config
                .set_max_write(1024 * 1024)
                .map(|_| ())
                .map_err(|_| EIO)
        }
    
        fn lookup(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, parent: u64, name: &OsStr, reply: ReplyEntry) {
            match self.namespace.lookup(parent, name) {
                Some(node) => reply.entry(&self.ttl, &self.attr(node, None), 0),
                None => reply.error(ENOENT),
            }
        }
    
        fn getattr(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, ino: u64, fh: Option<u64>, reply: ReplyAttr) {
            match self.namespace.node(ino) {
                Some(node) => {
                    let size = fh
                        .and_then(|fh| self.open_files.get(&fh))
                        .filter(|handle| handle.ino == ino)
                        .map(|handle| match &handle.completed {
                            Some(Ok(bytes)) | Some(Err((_, bytes))) => bytes.len() as u64,
                            None => handle.bytes.len() as u64,
                        });
                    reply.attr(&self.ttl, &self.attr(node, size));
                }
                None => reply.error(ENOENT),
            }
        }
    
        #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
        fn setattr(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            ino: u64,
            mode: Option<u32>,
            uid: Option<u32>,
            gid: Option<u32>,
            size: Option<u64>,
            _atime: Option<TimeOrNow>,
            _mtime: Option<TimeOrNow>,
            _ctime: Option<std::time::SystemTime>,
            fh: Option<u64>,
            _crtime: Option<std::time::SystemTime>,
            _chgtime: Option<std::time::SystemTime>,
            _bkuptime: Option<std::time::SystemTime>,
            _flags: Option<u32>,
            reply: ReplyAttr,
        ) {
            if mode.is_some() || uid.is_some() || gid.is_some() {
                reply.error(EROFS);
                return;
            }
            let Some(node) = self.namespace.node(ino) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            if !node_writable(node) {
                reply.error(EROFS);
                return;
            }
            let Some(size) = size else {
                reply.attr(&self.ttl, &self.attr(node, None));
                return;
            };
            let Some(fh) = fh else {
                reply.error(EACCES);
                return;
            };
            let Some(handle) = self.open_files.get_mut(&fh) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            if handle.ino != ino || handle.completed.is_some() {
                reply.error(EINVAL);
                return;
            }
            handle.bytes.resize(size as usize, 0);
            handle.dirty = true;
            reply.attr(&self.ttl, &self.attr(node, Some(size)));
        }
    
        fn readlink(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, ino: u64, reply: ReplyData) {
            match self.namespace.node(ino).map(|node| &node.kind) {
                Some(NodeKind::Symlink(target)) => reply.data(target.as_bytes()),
                Some(_) => reply.error(EINVAL),
                None => reply.error(ENOENT),
            }
        }
    
        fn open(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, ino: u64, flags: i32, reply: ReplyOpen) {
            let Some(node) = self.namespace.node(ino) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            let access = flags & libc::O_ACCMODE;
            let write_requested = access == libc::O_WRONLY || access == libc::O_RDWR;
    
            let content = match &node.kind {
                NodeKind::File(bytes) => {
                    if write_requested && node.write_target.is_none() {
                        reply.error(EROFS);
                        return;
                    }
                    let mut content = bytes.read().clone();
                    if write_requested && flags & libc::O_TRUNC != 0 {
                        content.clear();
                    }
                    content
                }
                NodeKind::LiveFile { .. } => {
                    // LiveFile is read-only; reject write opens.
                    if write_requested {
                        reply.error(EROFS);
                        return;
                    }
                    // Read SHM state once at open and snapshot into the handle.
                    // Reopening gets fresh state; the handle is stable until close.
                    let Some(content) = self.live_state_bytes(node) else {
                        reply.error(EIO);
                        return;
                    };
                    content
                }
                NodeKind::Directory => {
                    reply.error(EISDIR);
                    return;
                }
                NodeKind::Symlink(_) => {
                    reply.error(EINVAL);
                    return;
                }
                NodeKind::CallFile { .. } => Vec::new(),
                NodeKind::Outcome {
                    plugin_id,
                    method,
                    error,
                } => {
                    if write_requested {
                        reply.error(EROFS);
                        return;
                    }
                    self.outcome_bytes(plugin_id, method, *error)
                }
            };
    
            // A call file is dispatched only after real bytes arrive, so an open
            // that merely truncates never runs a call with empty arguments.
            let dirty = write_requested
                && flags & libc::O_TRUNC != 0
                && !matches!(node.kind, NodeKind::CallFile { .. });
            let fh = self.next_fh;
            self.next_fh = self.next_fh.wrapping_add(1).max(1);
            self.open_files.insert(
                fh,
                OpenFile {
                    ino,
                    bytes: content,
                    dirty,
                    completed: None,
                },
            );
            reply.opened(fh, fuser::consts::FOPEN_DIRECT_IO);
        }
    
        fn read(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            ino: u64,
            fh: u64,
            offset: i64,
            size: u32,
            _flags: i32,
            _lock_owner: Option<u64>,
            reply: ReplyData,
        ) {
            if offset < 0 {
                reply.error(EINVAL);
                return;
            }
            match self.read_bytes(ino, fh) {
                Ok(bytes) => {
                    let start = offset as usize;
                    if start >= bytes.len() {
                        reply.data(&[]);
                        return;
                    }
                    let end = start.saturating_add(size as usize).min(bytes.len());
                    reply.data(&bytes[start..end]);
                }
                Err(error) => reply.error(error),
            }
        }
    
        #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
        fn write(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            ino: u64,
            fh: u64,
            offset: i64,
            data: &[u8],
            _write_flags: u32,
            _flags: i32,
            _lock_owner: Option<u64>,
            reply: ReplyWrite,
        ) {
            if offset < 0 {
                reply.error(EINVAL);
                return;
            }
            let Some(node) = self.namespace.node(ino) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            if !node_writable(node) {
                reply.error(EROFS);
                return;
            }
            let Some(handle) = self.open_files.get_mut(&fh) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            if handle.ino != ino || handle.completed.is_some() {
                reply.error(EINVAL);
                return;
            }
            let start = offset as usize;
            if data.is_empty() {
                reply.written(0);
                return;
            }
            let end = match start.checked_add(data.len()) {
                Some(end) => end,
                None => {
                    reply.error(EINVAL);
                    return;
                }
            };
            if handle.bytes.len() < end {
                handle.bytes.resize(end, 0);
            }
            handle.bytes[start..end].copy_from_slice(data);
            handle.dirty = !handle.bytes.is_empty();
            reply.written(data.len() as u32);
        }
    
        fn flush(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            _ino: u64,
            fh: u64,
            _lock_owner: u64,
            reply: ReplyEmpty,
        ) {
            match self.flush_handle(fh) {
                Ok(()) => reply.ok(),
                Err(error) => reply.error(error),
            }
        }
    
        fn release(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            _ino: u64,
            fh: u64,
            _flags: i32,
            _lock_owner: Option<u64>,
            _flush: bool,
            reply: ReplyEmpty,
        ) {
            let result = self.flush_handle(fh);
            self.open_files.remove(&fh);
            match result {
                Ok(()) => reply.ok(),
                Err(error) => reply.error(error),
            }
        }
    
        fn fsync(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            _ino: u64,
            fh: u64,
            _datasync: bool,
            reply: ReplyEmpty,
        ) {
            match self.flush_handle(fh) {
                Ok(()) => reply.ok(),
                Err(error) => reply.error(error),
            }
        }
    
        fn readdir(
            &mut self,
            _request: &Request<'_>,
            ino: u64,
            _fh: u64,
            offset: i64,
            mut reply: ReplyDirectory,
        ) {
            let Some(node) = self.namespace.node(ino) else {
                reply.error(ENOENT);
                return;
            };
            if !matches!(node.kind, NodeKind::Directory) {
                reply.error(EINVAL);
                return;
            }
            let Some(children) = self.namespace.children(ino) else {
                reply.error(EIO);
                return;
            };
            let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(children.len() + 2);
            entries.push((ino, FileType::Directory, OsStr::new(".")));
            entries.push((node.parent, FileType::Directory, OsStr::new("..")));
            for (name, child_ino) in children {
                let child = &self.namespace.nodes[child_ino];
                let kind = match child.kind {
                    NodeKind::Directory => FileType::Directory,
                    NodeKind::File(_)
                    | NodeKind::LiveFile { .. }
                    | NodeKind::CallFile { .. }
                    | NodeKind::Outcome { .. } => FileType::RegularFile,
                    NodeKind::Symlink(_) => FileType::Symlink,
                };
                entries.push((*child_ino, kind, name.as_os_str()));
            }
    
            for (index, (child_ino, kind, name)) in
                entries.into_iter().enumerate().skip(offset.max(0) as usize)
            {
                if reply.add(child_ino, (index + 1) as i64, kind, name) {
                    break;
                }
            }
            reply.ok();
        }
    
        fn access(&mut self, _request: &Request<'_>, ino: u64, mask: i32, reply: ReplyEmpty) {
            match self.namespace.node(ino) {
                None => reply.error(ENOENT),
                Some(node) if mask & libc::W_OK != 0 && !node_writable(node) => reply.error(EROFS),
                Some(_) => reply.ok(),
            }
        }
    }

        fn attr(&self, node: &Node, size_override: Option<u64>) -> FileAttr {
            let (kind, size, perm, nlink) = match &node.kind {
                NodeKind::Directory => (FileType::Directory, 0, 0o555, 2),
                NodeKind::File(bytes) => (
                    FileType::RegularFile,
                    size_override.unwrap_or_else(|| bytes.read().len() as u64),
                    if node.write_target.is_some() {
                        0o644
                    } else {
                        0o444
                    },
                    1,
                ),
                NodeKind::LiveFile { .. } => {
                    let size = size_override.unwrap_or_else(|| {
                        self.live_state_bytes(node)
                            .map(|b| b.len() as u64)
                            .unwrap_or(0)
                    });
                    (FileType::RegularFile, size, 0o444, 1)
                }
                NodeKind::Symlink(target) => (FileType::Symlink, target.len() as u64, 0o777, 1),
                // Receipts are readable only through the handle that ran the call.
                NodeKind::CallFile { .. } => {
                    (FileType::RegularFile, size_override.unwrap_or(0), 0o666, 1)
                }
                NodeKind::Outcome {
                    plugin_id,
                    method,
                    error,
                } => {
                    let size = size_override
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.outcome_bytes(plugin_id, method, *error).len() as u64);
                    (FileType::RegularFile, size, 0o444, 1)
                }
            };
            FileAttr {
                ino: node.ino,
                size,
                blocks: size.div_ceil(512),
                atime: UNIX_EPOCH,
                mtime: UNIX_EPOCH,
                ctime: UNIX_EPOCH,
                crtime: UNIX_EPOCH,
                kind,
                perm,
                nlink,
                uid: self.uid,
                gid: self.gid,
                rdev: 0,
                flags: 0,
                blksize: 4096,
            }

        /// Read a plugin's live state from SHM and extract the value at the given
        /// JSON pointer, as pretty-printed JSON bytes. Rendering happens once per
        /// committed state version; later opens and size checks reuse it.
        fn live_state_bytes(&self, node: &Node) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
            let (plugin_id, pointer) = match &node.kind {
                NodeKind::LiveFile { plugin_id, pointer } => (plugin_id.as_str(), pointer.as_str()),
                _ => return None,
            };
            let state_dir = self.namespace.state_dir.as_ref()?;
            let path = state_dir.join(format!("{plugin_id}.json"));
            let key = StateKey::of(&std::fs::metadata(&path).ok()?);
            let cache_key = (plugin_id.to_string(), pointer.to_string());
            if let Some((cached, bytes)) = self.live_cache.lock().get(&cache_key)
                && *cached == key
            {
                return Some(bytes.clone());
            }
            let raw = std::fs::read(&path).ok()?;
            let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).ok()?;
            let extracted = if pointer.is_empty() {
                value
            } else {
                value.pointer(pointer).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
            };
            let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&extracted).ok()?;
            bytes.push(b'\n');
            // A commit that lands between the stat and the read is stored under
            // the older key, so the next open simply renders it again.
            self.live_cache
                .lock()
                .insert(cache_key, (key, bytes.clone()));
            Some(bytes)
        }
    
        fn refresh_namespace(&mut self) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
            let state_dir = self.namespace.state_dir.clone();
            self.namespace = Namespace::build_with(
                &self.store,
                self.namespace.target.clone(),
                state_dir.as_deref(),
                self.namespace.lungs,
            )?;

                && !session.is_empty()
            {
                self.namespace.declare_socket_session(session)?;
            }

        fn flush_handle(&mut self, fh: u64) -> Result<(), i32> {
            let Some(handle) = self.open_files.get_mut(&fh) else {
                return Err(ENOENT);
            };
            if let Some(completed) = &handle.completed {
                return completed.as_ref().map(|_| ()).map_err(|(errno, _)| *errno);
            }
            if !handle.dirty {
                return Ok(());
            }
            let node = self.namespace.node(handle.ino).ok_or(ENOENT)?;
            if let NodeKind::CallFile { plugin_id, method } = &node.kind {
                // Clear dirty first: release flushes again, and a call must run
                // once per complete write even when it fails.
                handle.dirty = false;
                if handle.bytes.is_empty() {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                let bytes = std::mem::take(&mut handle.bytes);
                let (plugin_id, method) = (plugin_id.clone(), method.clone());
                let completed = self.lungs_call(&plugin_id, &method, &bytes);
                let result = completed.as_ref().map(|_| ()).map_err(|(errno, _)| *errno);
                self.open_files.get_mut(&fh).ok_or(ENOENT)?.completed = Some(completed);
                return result;
            }
            let target = node.write_target.clone().ok_or(EROFS)?;
            let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&handle.bytes).map_err(|_| EINVAL)?;
            self.store
                .stage_pointer(
                    &target.workspace_id,
                    &target.plugin_id,
                    &target.pointer,
                    value,
                )
                .map_err(|_| EINVAL)?;
            handle.dirty = false;
            self.refresh_namespace().map_err(|_| EIO)?;
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn read_bytes(&self, ino: u64, fh: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, i32> {
            if let Some(handle) = self.open_files.get(&fh)
                && handle.ino == ino
            {
                if matches!(
                    self.namespace.node(ino).ok_or(ENOENT)?.kind,
                    NodeKind::CallFile { .. }
                ) {
                    return Ok(match &handle.completed {
                        Some(Ok(receipt)) => receipt.clone(),
                        Some(Err((_, diagnostic))) => diagnostic.clone(),
                        None => Vec::new(),
                    });
                }
                return Ok(handle.bytes.clone());
            }
            match &self.namespace.node(ino).ok_or(ENOENT)?.kind {
                NodeKind::File(bytes) => Ok(bytes.read().clone()),
                NodeKind::LiveFile { .. } => {
                    let node = self.namespace.node(ino).ok_or(ENOENT)?;
                    self.live_state_bytes(node).ok_or(EIO)
                }
                NodeKind::Directory => Err(EISDIR),
                NodeKind::Symlink(_) => Err(EINVAL),
                NodeKind::CallFile { .. } => Ok(Vec::new()),
                NodeKind::Outcome {
                    plugin_id,
                    method,
                    error,
                } => Ok(self.outcome_bytes(plugin_id, method, *error)),
            }
        }
    }

        pub(crate) fn declare_socket_session(&mut self, session: &str) -> Result<()> {
            let node = self
                .lookup(ROOT_INO, std::ffi::OsStr::new(".3tchedfs.json"))
                .context("mount metadata missing")?;
            let NodeKind::File(bytes) = &node.kind else {
                bail!("mount metadata is not a file")

            let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes.read())?;
            value["session_id"] = Value::String(session.to_owned());

            rendered.push(b'\n');

            Ok(())
        }

        fn add_node(
            &mut self,
            parent: u64,
            name: &str,
            kind: NodeKind,
            write_target: Option<WriteTarget>,
        ) -> Result<u64> {
            let parent_node = self
                .namespace
                .nodes
                .get(&parent)
                .with_context(|| format!("parent inode {parent} does not exist"))?;
            if !matches!(parent_node.kind, NodeKind::Directory) {
                bail!("parent {} is not a directory", parent_node.path);
            }
            let path = if parent_node.path == "/" {
                format!("/{name}")
            } else {
                format!("{}/{}", parent_node.path, name)
            };
            if self.paths.contains_key(&path) {
                bail!("duplicate namespace path {path}");
            }
            let ino = inode_for_path(&path);
            if let Some(existing) = self.namespace.nodes.get(&ino) {
                bail!("inode collision between {} and {path}", existing.path);
            }
            let node = Node {
                ino,
                parent,
                name: OsString::from(name),
                path: path.clone(),
                kind,
                write_target,
            };
            if matches!(node.kind, NodeKind::Directory) {
                self.namespace.children.insert(ino, BTreeMap::new());
            }
            self.namespace
                .children
                .entry(parent)
                .or_default()
                .insert(node.name.clone(), ino);
            self.namespace.nodes.insert(ino, node);
            self.paths.insert(path, ino);
            Ok(ino)
        }

    fn pointer_is_immutable(
        schema: Option<&PluginSchema>,
        pointer: &str,
        field: Option<&FieldSchema>,
        _root_value: &Value,
    ) -> bool {
        let Some(schema) = schema else {
            return false;
        };
        if field.is_some_and(|field| field.read_only) {
            return true;
        }
        // Conditional writability depends on a sibling in the full plugin value.
        // Keep such leaves read-only in the direct file projection; whole-state
        // staging can still evaluate the condition accurately.
        if field.is_some_and(|field| field.read_only_when.is_some()) {
            return true;
        }
        schema
            .immutable_paths
            .iter()
            .any(|immutable| pointer == immutable || pointer.starts_with(&format!("{immutable}/")))
    }

                .filter(|id| !id.is_empty())

                ensure!(
                    session == expected,
                    "mounted identity session differs from --expected-session"

                "view_id",

                .read(true)
                .custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW)
                .open(&self.path)
                .context("reopen mount root")?;

            let present = current.metadata()?;
            ensure!(

                "3tchedFS root changed"

                "3tchedFS identity or catalog declaration changed"

                "3tchedFS view changed"

        pub fn current_view_id(&self) -> Result<Option<String>> {
            let path = self.root.join("current");
            match fs::read_to_string(&path) {
                Ok(value) => Ok(Some(value.trim().to_string())),
                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
                Err(error) => Err(error).with_context(|| format!("read {}", path.display())),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn current_view(&self) -> Option<Result<ViewManifest>> {
            match self.current_view_id() {
                Ok(Some(id)) => Some(self.read_view(&id)),
                Ok(None) => None,
                Err(error) => Some(Err(error)),
            }
        }
    
        pub fn read_view(&self, id: &str) -> Result<ViewManifest> {
            validate_hash(id, "view")?;
            let view: ViewManifest = self.read_json(self.view_path(id))?;
            if view.view_id != id {
                bail!(
                    "view file identity mismatch: requested {id}, contains {}",
                    view.view_id
                );
            }
            let actual = hash_json(&ViewBody {
                format: view.format.clone(),
                source_catalog_hash: view.source_catalog_hash.clone(),
                source_catalog_generation: view.source_catalog_generation,
                parent_view: view.parent_view.clone(),
                objects: view.objects.clone(),
            })?;
            if actual != id {
                bail!("view {id} failed content-hash verification");
            }
            Ok(view)
        }
    
        pub fn read_object(&self, hash: &str) -> Result<TypedObjectBlob> {
            validate_hash(hash, "object")?;
            let path = self.object_path(hash);
            let bytes = fs::read(&path).with_context(|| format!("read {}", path.display()))?;
            if hash_bytes(&bytes) != hash {
                bail!("object {hash} failed content-hash verification");
            }
            let object: TypedObjectBlob =
                serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).with_context(|| format!("decode object {hash}"))?;
            object.validate(None)?;
            Ok(object)
        }

            let hash = view
                .objects
                .get(plugin_id)
                .with_context(|| format!("plugin '{plugin_id}' is not in view {}", view.view_id))?;
            self.read_object(hash)
        }
    
        pub fn workspace_object(

            workspace: &Workspace,
            plugin_id: &str,

            let view = ViewManifest {

            }
