        }
    
        fn atomic_json(&self, path: &Path, value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<()> {
            self.atomic_write(path, &canonical_json(value)?)
        }
    
        fn atomic_write(&self, path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
            let parent = path.parent().context("atomic write path has no parent")?;
            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
            let temp = parent.join(format!(
                ".{}.{}.tmp",
                path.file_name()
                    .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
                    .unwrap_or("object"),
                Uuid::new_v4()
            ));
            {
                let mut file = File::create(&temp)
                    .with_context(|| format!("create temporary file {}", temp.display()))?;
                file.write_all(bytes)?;
                file.sync_all()?;
            }
            fs::rename(&temp, path)
                .with_context(|| format!("publish {} -> {}", temp.display(), path.display()))?;
            File::open(parent)?.sync_all()?;
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn read_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(&self, path: PathBuf) -> Result<T> {
            let bytes = fs::read(&path).with_context(|| format!("read {}", path.display()))?;
            serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).with_context(|| format!("decode {}", path.display()))
        }
    
        fn lock_exclusive(&self) -> Result<StoreLock> {
            let path = self.root.join(".lock");
            let file = OpenOptions::new()
                .create(true)
                .truncate(false)
                .read(true)
                .write(true)
                .open(&path)
                .with_context(|| format!("open store lock {}", path.display()))?;
            file.lock_exclusive()
                .with_context(|| format!("lock store {}", self.root.display()))?;
            Ok(StoreLock(file))
        }
    
        fn objects_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.root.join("objects")
        }
    
        fn views_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.root.join("views")
        }
    
        fn workspaces_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.root.join("workspaces")
        }
    
        fn snapshots_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
            self.root.join("snapshots")
        }
    
        fn object_path(&self, hash: &str) -> PathBuf {
            self.objects_dir().join(format!("{hash}.blob"))
        }
    
        fn view_path(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
            self.views_dir().join(format!("{id}.json"))
        }
    
        fn workspace_path(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
            self.workspaces_dir().join(format!("{id}.json"))
        }
    
        fn snapshot_path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
            self.snapshots_dir().join(format!("{name}.ref"))
        }
    }
    
    struct StoreLock(File);
    
    impl Drop for StoreLock {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = self.0.unlock();
        }
    }
    
    fn canonical_json(value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        serde_json::to_vec(value).context("serialize canonical JSON")
    }
    
    fn hash_json(value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<String> {
        Ok(hash_bytes(&canonical_json(value)?))
    }

        blake3::hash(bytes).to_hex().to_string()

    const PLUGIN_INTERFACE: &str = "org.opdbus.v1.PluginV1";

    const IDENTITY_OBJECT_PATH: &str = "/org/opdbus/v1/identity/dbus";
    const IDENTITY_INTERFACE: &str = "org.opdbus.v1.DbusIdentityV1";
    /// Mirrors the bridge's registration bound; larger files are not SID1.
    const MAX_CREDENTIAL_BYTES: u64 = 16 * 1024;
    /// The bridge's lungs bootstrap: a connection binds to one session here first.
    const LUNGS_OBJECT_PATH: &str = "/org/opdbus/v1/lungs";
    const LUNGS_INTERFACE: &str = "org.opdbus.v1.LungsV1";

    #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
    pub struct CallReceipt {
        pub plugin_id: String,
        pub method: String,
        pub subid: String,
        pub required_capability: Option<String>,
        pub side_effect: SideEffect,
        pub idempotent: bool,
        pub result: Value,
    }
    
    /// Why a lungs call did not complete. Each stage maps to one errno so the
    /// writer learns what failed from `close()`, and the full text goes to the
    /// method's `error` file.
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum LungsError {
        #[error("arguments are not a JSON value: {0}")]
        Json(String),
        #[error("arguments failed schema validation: {0}")]
        Arguments(String),
        #[error("no credential has been delivered to this identity: {0}")]
        Credential(String),
        #[error("identity registration refused: {0}")]
        Registration(String),
        #[error("call refused: {0}")]
        Refused(String),
        #[error("dispatch failed: {0}")]
        Transport(String),
    }
    
    impl LungsError {
        pub fn stage(&self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Self::Json(_) => "parse",
                Self::Arguments(_) => "validate",
                Self::Credential(_) => "credential",
                Self::Registration(_) => "register",
                Self::Refused(_) => "call",
                Self::Transport(_) => "transport",
            }
        }
    
        pub fn errno(&self) -> i32 {
            match self {
                Self::Json(_) | Self::Arguments(_) => libc::EINVAL,
                Self::Credential(_) | Self::Registration(_) | Self::Refused(_) => libc::EACCES,
                Self::Transport(_) => libc::EIO,
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn method_decl(
        store: &ObjectStore,
        target: &ProjectionTarget,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<MethodDecl> {
        let object = match target {
            ProjectionTarget::View(id) => {
                let view = store.read_view(id)?;
                store.object_for_view(&view, plugin_id)?
            }
            ProjectionTarget::Workspace(id) => {
                let workspace = store.read_workspace(id)?;
                store.workspace_object(&workspace, plugin_id)?
            }
        };
        object
            .schema
            .methods
            .get(method_name)
            .cloned()
            .with_context(|| format!("method '{plugin_id}.{method_name}' is not schema-declared"))
    }
    
    pub fn validate_arguments(method: &MethodDecl, arguments: &Value) -> Result<(), LungsError> {
        jsonschema::Validator::new(&method.args)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Arguments(format!("sealed argument schema: {error}")))?
            .validate(arguments)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Arguments(error.to_string()))
    }
    
    /// Read the identity's SID1 from its own device. It is read per call, so a
    /// delivered or refreshed credential takes effect without a remount.
    pub fn read_credential(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, LungsError> {
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Credential(format!("{}: {error}", path.display())))?;
        if !metadata.is_file() || metadata.len() == 0 || metadata.len() > MAX_CREDENTIAL_BYTES {
            return Err(LungsError::Credential(format!(
                "{} is not a SID1 credential file",
                path.display()
            )));
        }
        let bytes = std::fs::read(path)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Credential(format!("{}: {error}", path.display())))?;
        if !bytes.starts_with(b"SID1") {
            return Err(LungsError::Credential(format!(
                "{} does not hold a SID1 envelope",
                path.display()
            )));
        }
        Ok(bytes)
    }
    
    pub async fn call(
        store: &ObjectStore,
        target: &ProjectionTarget,
        bus_address: &str,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        arguments: Value,
        confirm_side_effects: bool,
    ) -> Result<CallReceipt> {
        let method = method_decl(store, target, plugin_id, method_name)?;
        validate_arguments(&method, &arguments)?;
    
        if method.side_effect != SideEffect::Read && !confirm_side_effects {
            bail!(
                "'{plugin_id}.{method_name}' is a {:?} operation; pass --confirm-side-effects",
                method.side_effect
            );
        }
    
        let connection = zbus::connection::Builder::address(bus_address)?
            .build()
            .await
            .with_context(|| format!("connect to D-Bus at {bus_address}"))?;
        let result = plugin_call(&connection, plugin_id, method_name, &arguments)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("dispatch '{plugin_id}.{method_name}': {error}"))?;
        Ok(receipt(plugin_id, method_name, &method, result))
    }
    
    /// Dispatch as the identity that owns the lungs mount. Registration and the
    /// call share one connection, so the bridge admits the call as that identity
    /// and runs it through MutationEngine under the identity's own grants.
    pub async fn call_as_identity(
        bus_address: &str,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        method: &MethodDecl,
        arguments: Value,
        credential: Vec<u8>,
    ) -> Result<CallReceipt, LungsError> {
        let connection = zbus::connection::Builder::address(bus_address)
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("bus address {bus_address}: {error}")))?
            .build()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("connect to {bus_address}: {error}")))?;
        let bootstrap = Proxy::new(
            &connection,
            PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
            IDENTITY_OBJECT_PATH,
            IDENTITY_INTERFACE,
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("identity bootstrap proxy: {error}")))?;
        let registered: bool = bootstrap
            .call("RegisterCurrentSender", &(credential,))
            .await
            .map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
                true => LungsError::Registration(error.to_string()),
                false => LungsError::Transport(format!("register: {error}")),
            })?;
        if !registered {
            return Err(LungsError::Registration(
                "bridge declined the credential".into(),
            ));
        }
        let result = plugin_call(&connection, plugin_id, method_name, &arguments)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
                true => LungsError::Refused(error.to_string()),
                false => LungsError::Transport(format!("call: {error}")),
            })?;
        Ok(receipt(plugin_id, method_name, method, result))
    }

            .await
            .map_err(|error| {
                LungsError::Transport(format!("connect to {}: {error}", socket.display()))
            })?;
        let connection = tokio::time::timeout(
            LUNGS_NEGOTIATION_TIMEOUT,
            zbus::connection::Builder::unix_stream(stream)
                .p2p()
                .auth_mechanism(zbus::connection::AuthMechanism::Anonymous)
                .build(),
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|_| LungsError::Transport("lungs socket negotiation timed out".into()))?
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("lungs socket: {error}")))?;
        let lungs = Proxy::new(
            &connection,
            PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
            LUNGS_OBJECT_PATH,
            LUNGS_INTERFACE,
        )
        .await
        .map_err(|error| LungsError::Transport(format!("lungs bind proxy: {error}")))?;
        let binding = if session.is_empty() {
            lungs.call("BindCurrentContainer", &()).await
        } else {
            lungs.call("Bind", &(session,)).await
        };
        let bound: bool = binding.map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
            true => LungsError::Registration(error.to_string()),
            false => LungsError::Transport(format!("bind: {error}")),
        })?;
        if !bound {
            return Err(LungsError::Registration(
                "bridge declined to bind this session".into(),
            ));
        }
        let result = plugin_call(&connection, plugin_id, method_name, &arguments)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| match refusal(&error) {
                true => LungsError::Refused(error.to_string()),
                false => LungsError::Transport(format!("call: {error}")),
            })?;
        Ok(receipt(plugin_id, method_name, method, result))
    }
    
    async fn plugin_call(
        connection: &zbus::Connection,
        plugin_id: &str,
        method_name: &str,
        arguments: &Value,
    ) -> zbus::Result<Value> {
        let proxy = Proxy::new(
            connection,
            PLUGIN_BUS_NAME,
            format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id}"),
            PLUGIN_INTERFACE,
        )
        .await?;
        let json_args = serde_json::to_string(arguments)
            .map_err(|error| zbus::Error::Failure(format!("serialize arguments: {error}")))?;
        let response: String = proxy
            .call("Call", &(method_name.to_string(), json_args))
            .await?;
        Ok(serde_json::from_str(&response).unwrap_or(Value::String(response)))
    }
    
    fn refusal(error: &zbus::Error) -> bool {
        matches!(error, zbus::Error::MethodError(name, _, _)
            if name.as_str() == "org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied")
            || matches!(error, zbus::Error::FDO(fdo) if matches!(**fdo, zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied(_)))
    }
    
    fn receipt(plugin_id: &str, method_name: &str, method: &MethodDecl, result: Value) -> CallReceipt {
        CallReceipt {
            plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),
            method: method_name.to_string(),
            subid: method.subid.clone(),
            required_capability: method.required_capability.clone(),
            side_effect: method.side_effect,
            idempotent: method.idempotent,
            result,
        }
    }

    fn field_for_pointer<'a>(
        plugin_schema: Option<&'a PluginSchema>,
        parent: Option<&'a FieldSchema>,
        name: &str,
    ) -> Option<&'a FieldSchema> {
        fn object_field<'a>(field_type: &'a FieldType, name: &str) -> Option<&'a FieldSchema> {
            match field_type {
                FieldType::Object(fields) => fields.get(name),
                FieldType::Array(item) => object_field(item, name),
                _ => None,
            }
        }
    
        match parent.and_then(|field| object_field(&field.field_type, name)) {
            Some(field) => Some(field),
            None if parent.is_none() => plugin_schema.and_then(|schema| schema.fields.get(name)),
            None => None,
        }
    }
    
    fn push_pointer(parent: &str, segment: &str) -> String {
        let escaped = segment.replace('~', "~0").replace('/', "~1");
        format!("{parent}/{escaped}")
    }
    
    pub fn encode_component(value: &str) -> String {
        let mut output = String::new();
        for byte in value.bytes() {
            if byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'.' | b'_' | b'-') {
                output.push(byte as char);
            } else {
                output.push_str(&format!("%{byte:02X}"));
            }
        }
        if output == "." || output == ".." || output.is_empty() {
            format!("%{}", hex_bytes(value.as_bytes()))
        } else {
            output
        }
    }
    
    fn hex_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
        bytes.iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02X}")).collect()
    }
    
    fn inode_for_path(path: &str) -> u64 {
        let bytes = blake3::hash(path.as_bytes()).as_bytes()[..8]
            .try_into()
            .expect("eight-byte slice");
        let mut ino = u64::from_le_bytes(bytes) | (1 << 63);
        if ino == ROOT_INO {
            ino += 1;
        }
        ino
    }

    impl FieldSchema {
        pub fn validate(&self, value: &Value, root: &Value) -> Result<()> {
            // PluginSchema represents `Option<T>` as a non-required T while live
            // state may preserve an explicit JSON null for that option.
            if value.is_null() && !self.required {
                return Ok(());
            }
            self.field_type.validate(value, root)?;
            for constraint in &self.constraints {
                constraint.validate(value, root)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        pub fn template(&self) -> Value {
            self.default
                .clone()
                .or_else(|| self.example.clone())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| self.field_type.template())
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum FieldType {
        String,
        Integer,
        Float,
        Boolean,
        Array(Box<FieldType>),
        Object(BTreeMap<String, FieldSchema>),
        /// Dynamic string keys with one declared value type. Wire form matches
        /// op-state-store: `{"map": <FieldType>}`.
        Map(Box<FieldType>),
        /// Explicit exact JSON Schema document retained from the sealed plugin.
        /// Wire form matches op-state-store: `{"json_schema": <document>}`.
        JsonSchema(Box<Value>),
        Enum(Vec<String>),
        OneOf(Vec<FieldType>),
        Any,
    }
    
    impl FieldType {
        pub fn validate(&self, value: &Value, root: &Value) -> Result<()> {
            match self {
                Self::String if !value.is_string() => bail!("expected string"),
                Self::Integer if !value.is_i64() && !value.is_u64() => bail!("expected integer"),
                Self::Float if !value.is_number() => bail!("expected number"),
                Self::Boolean if !value.is_boolean() => bail!("expected boolean"),
                Self::Array(item_type) => {
                    let values = value.as_array().context("expected array")?;
                    for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
                        item_type
                            .validate(value, root)
                            .with_context(|| format!("array element {index}"))?;
                    }
                }
                Self::Object(fields) => {
                    let object = value.as_object().context("expected object")?;
                    for (name, field) in fields {
                        match object.get(name) {
                            Some(value) => field
                                .validate(value, root)
                                .with_context(|| format!("object field {name}"))?,
                            None if field.required => bail!("required object field {name} is missing"),
                            None => {}
                        }
                    }
                }
                Self::Map(item_type) => {
                    let object = value.as_object().context("expected object map")?;
                    for (index, value) in object.values().enumerate() {
                        // Dynamic keys may be private; keep errors key-agnostic.
                        item_type
                            .validate(value, root)
                            .with_context(|| format!("map value {index}"))?;
                    }
                }
                Self::JsonSchema(schema) => {
                    jsonschema::Validator::new(schema)
                        .context("compile embedded json_schema field")?
                        .validate(value)
                        .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("value failed json_schema: {error}"))?;
                }
                Self::Enum(variants) => {
                    let value = value.as_str().context("expected enum string")?;
                    if !variants.iter().any(|variant| variant == value) {
                        bail!("'{value}' is not an allowed enum value");
                    }
                }
                Self::OneOf(branches) => {
                    let matches = branches
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|branch| branch.validate(value, root).is_ok())
                        .count();
                    // The current schemars adapter reduces some discriminated
                    // variants to the same FieldType shape. Require at least one
                    // matching branch; the sealed JSON Schema remains available
                    // in the object for stricter discriminator-aware consumers.
                    if matches == 0 {
                        bail!("value does not match any union branch");
                    }
                }
                Self::Any | Self::String | Self::Integer | Self::Float | Self::Boolean => {}
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        pub fn template(&self) -> Value {
            match self {
                Self::String => Value::String(String::new()),
                Self::Integer => Value::from(0),
                Self::Float => Value::from(0.0),
                Self::Boolean => Value::Bool(false),
                Self::Array(_) => Value::Array(Vec::new()),
                Self::Object(fields) => Value::Object(
                    fields
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(name, field)| (name.clone(), field.template()))
                        .collect(),
                ),
                Self::Map(_) => Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),
                Self::JsonSchema(schema) => json_schema_template(schema),
                Self::Any => Value::Null,
                Self::Enum(values) => values
                    .first()
                    .cloned()
                    .map(Value::String)
                    .unwrap_or(Value::Null),
                Self::OneOf(branches) => branches.first().map(Self::template).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
            }
        }
    }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
    #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum Constraint {
        Min { value: f64 },
        Max { value: f64 },
        Pattern { regex: String },
        OneOf { values: Vec<Value> },
        RequiresField { field: String },
        Custom { validator: String },
    }
    
    impl Constraint {
        fn validate(&self, value: &Value, root: &Value) -> Result<()> {
            match self {
                Self::Min { value: minimum } => {
                    let actual = measure(value).context("min constraint requires number or length")?;
                    if actual < *minimum {
                        bail!("{actual} is below minimum {minimum}");
                    }
                }
                Self::Max { value: maximum } => {
                    let actual = measure(value).context("max constraint requires number or length")?;
                    if actual > *maximum {
                        bail!("{actual} exceeds maximum {maximum}");
                    }
                }
                Self::Pattern { regex } => {
                    let actual = value
                        .as_str()
                        .context("pattern constraint requires string")?;
                    if !Regex::new(regex)
                        .with_context(|| format!("invalid schema regex '{regex}'"))?
                        .is_match(actual)
                    {
                        bail!("value does not match pattern '{regex}'");
                    }
                }
                Self::OneOf { values } if !values.contains(value) => {
                    bail!("value is not in the allowed set");
                }
                Self::RequiresField { field } if root.get(field).is_none() => {
                    bail!("required peer field '{field}' is missing");
                }
                // A custom validator names plugin code that this standalone
                // projection cannot execute. The plugin dispatch path remains the
                // final authority when a staged value is applied.
                Self::Custom { .. } | Self::OneOf { .. } | Self::RequiresField { .. } => {}
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    // Conversion from the sealed authority.
    //
    // `op_state_store::PluginSchema` decodes the sealed JSON; the functions below
    // turn it into this crate's view. Every struct is destructured by name and
    // every enum is matched without a wildcard, so when the authority gains a
    // field or a field type this crate stops compiling until it handles it. That
    // is how a new sealed field type can no longer break capture at run time.
    
    /// Convert a schema decoded by its authority into this crate's view.
    pub fn from_sealed(sealed: op_state_store::PluginSchema) -> Result<PluginSchema> {
        let op_state_store::PluginSchema {
            name,
            category,
            version,
            description,
            display_name,
            fields,
            public_state,
            field_writes,
            dependencies,
            example,
            immutable_paths,
            tags,
            dialect,
            mutation_index,
            subids,
            org,
            methods,
            capabilities,
            capability_grants,
            signals,
            guarantees,
        } = sealed;
        let op_state_store::PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback,
            supports_checkpoints,
            supports_verification,
            atomic_operations,
        } = guarantees;
        Ok(PluginSchema {
            name,
            category,
            version,
            description,
            display_name,
            fields: sealed_fields(fields)?,
            dependencies,
            immutable_paths,
            tags,
            dialect,
            mutation_index,
    }
    
    fn validate_hash(value: &str, kind: &str) -> Result<()> {
        if value.len() != 64 || !value.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
            bail!("invalid {kind} hash '{value}'");
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn validate_name(value: &str, kind: &str) -> Result<()> {
        if value.is_empty()
            || value.len() > 128
            || value == "."
            || value == ".."
            || !value
                .bytes()
                .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"._-".contains(&byte))
        {
            bail!("invalid {kind} name '{value}'");
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn list_stems(directory: &Path, suffix: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        let mut values = Vec::new();
        for entry in fs::read_dir(directory)
            .with_context(|| format!("list directory {}", directory.display()))?
        {
            let entry = entry?;
            if let Some(name) = entry.file_name().to_str()
                && let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(suffix)
            {
                values.push(stem.to_string());
            }
        }
        values.sort();
        Ok(values)
    }

    deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
    routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.

    - **Priority buckets:** Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff.

      or a Claude Code subagent (`Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`, `claude`).
    - **Dispatch:** tell Claude *"dispatch <ID> to <agent>"* — it spawns that agent with the task
      context and updates Status here when done.
    - **Add work:** append a row under the right bucket with a fresh `OD-##` id.

       434    /// Consistent snapshot with an aggregate byte budget, checked before each read.
       435    /// An over-budget snapshot fails as a whole; it never looks like missing state.
       436    pub fn read_projection_snapshot_bounded_in(
       437        state_dir: &str,
       438        plugin_ids: &[String],
       439        maximum_bytes: u64,
       440    ) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
       441        for plugin in plugin_ids {
       442            filename(plugin)?;
       443        }
       444        let Some(locked) = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, false)? else {
       445            return Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
       446                generation: 0,
       447                states: BTreeMap::new(),
       448            });
       449        };
       450        read_locked_snapshot_bounded(&locked, plugin_ids, maximum_bytes)
       451    }
       452
       453    fn read_locked_snapshot(
       454        locked: &LockedDirectory,
       455        plugin_ids: &[String],
       456    ) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
       457        read_locked_snapshot_bounded(locked, plugin_ids, u64::MAX)

       459
       460    fn read_locked_snapshot_bounded(
       461        locked: &LockedDirectory,
       462        plugin_ids: &[String],
       463        maximum_bytes: u64,
       464    ) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
       465        let Some((manifest, _)) = locked.manifest()? else {
       466            // Uncommitted files beside a missing manifest are not state authority.
       467            return Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
       468                generation: 0,
       469                states: BTreeMap::new(),
       470            });
       471        };
       472        let mut states = BTreeMap::new();
       473        let mut remaining = maximum_bytes;
       474        for plugin in plugin_ids {
       475            manifest.require_available(plugin)?;
       476            if let Some(bytes) = read_file(
       477                &locked.directory,
       478                &filename(plugin)?,
       479                MAX_PROJECTION.min(remaining),
       480                false,
       481            )? {
       482                remaining = remaining
       483                    .checked_sub(bytes.len() as u64)
       484                    .context("projection snapshot exceeds aggregate byte budget")?;
       485                states.insert(plugin.clone(), bytes);
       486            }
       487        }
       488        Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
       489            generation: manifest.generation,
       490            states,
       491        })
       492    }

    fn terminal_receipt(
        body: &str,
        synced: std::io::Result<()>,
        plugin: &str,
        method: &str,
        decl: &MethodDecl,
    ) -> Result<Value> {
        let value: Value =
            serde_json::from_str(body).context("missing or malformed terminal operation receipt")?;
        if value.get("error").is_some() {
            ensure!(
                value["plugin"] == plugin && value["method"] == method,
                "operation diagnostic attribution mismatch"
            );
            return Err(MountedDiagnostic(value).into());
        }
        ensure!(
            value["plugin_id"] == plugin && value["method"] == method,
            "operation receipt attribution mismatch"
        );
        synced.context("operation fsync failed without a terminal diagnostic")?;
        ensure!(
            value["subid"] == decl.subid
                && value["required_capability"] == serde_json::to_value(&decl.required_capability)?
                && value["side_effect"] == serde_json::to_value(decl.side_effect)?
                && value["idempotent"] == decl.idempotent,
            "operation receipt contract mismatch"
        );
        ensure!(
            value.get("result").is_some(),
            "terminal operation receipt has no result"
        );
        Ok(value)
    }

    //! Generate Rust bindings from the filesystem inventory, not from a second plugin schema.
    use std::fmt::Write as _;
    use std::io::Write as _;
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail, ensure};
    use serde_json::Value;
    
    fn identifier(value: &str) -> Result<&str> {
        ensure!(
            !value.is_empty()
                && value.bytes().enumerate().all(|(i, c)| c == b'_' || c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || (i > 0 && c.is_ascii_digit())),
            "invalid Rust identifier {value:?}"
        );
        Ok(value)
    }
    fn string<'a>(value: &'a Value, key: &str) -> Result<&'a str> {
        value[key].as_str().with_context(|| format!("missing string {key}"))
    }
    fn generate(schema: &Value) -> Result<String> {
        let types = schema["types"].as_object().context("missing types object")?;
        let classes = schema["bindings"]["classes"].as_object().context("missing bindings.classes")?;
        // Final inventory methods are reviewed independently of code-generation handler choices.
        if let Some(methods) = schema.get("methods") {
            for method in methods.as_array().context("methods must be a flat array")? {
                for key in ["name", "receiver", "route"] {
                    ensure!(method.get(key).is_some(), "method is missing {key}");
                }
            }
        }
        let mut out = String::from("// @generated by examples/typed_generate.rs from docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json.\n// Do not edit; this is a derived filesystem binding, never a plugin schema authority.\n#![allow(dead_code)]\nuse crate::typed_runtime::{NodeHandle, NodeError};\n");
        for (name, spec) in types {
            ensure!(spec["source_refs"].as_array().is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty()), "{name} has no source evidence");
            if name.contains('<') {
                ensure!(name == "BlobRef<T>" || name == "ShmHandle<T>", "unsupported generic type {name}");
            } else { identifier(name)?; }
            writeln!(out, "/// Source: {}", spec["source_refs"])?;
            match string(spec, "kind")? {
                "alias" => { writeln!(out, "pub type {name} = {};", string(spec,"rust")?)?; }
                "struct" => {
                    writeln!(out, "#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]\npub struct {name} {{")?;
                    for (field, ty) in spec["fields"].as_object().context("missing fields")? {
                        writeln!(out, "pub {}: {},", identifier(field)?, ty.as_str().context("field type must be string")?)?;
                    }
                    writeln!(out,"}}")?;
                }
                "enum" => {
                    writeln!(out, "#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum {name} {{")?;
                    for (variant, ty) in spec["variants"].as_object().context("missing variants")? {
                        writeln!(out,"{}({}),",identifier(variant)?,ty.as_str().context("variant type must be string")?)?;
                    }
                    writeln!(out,"}}")?;
                }
                "validated_string" => {
                    let validator = identifier(string(spec,"validator")?)?;
                    writeln!(out,"#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub struct {name}(String);\nimpl {name} {{ pub fn new(value: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {{ let value=value.into(); crate::typed_runtime::validate_{validator}(&value)?; Ok(Self(value)) }} pub fn as_str(&self)->&str {{ &self.0 }} }}")?;
                }
                "recursive_json" => {

    /// Binding-defined conditions preserve source I/O codes as diagnostics, not a bare errno API.
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum NodeError {
        #[error("binding contract: {0}")]
        Contract(String),
        #[error("{operation}: {message} ({kind:?}, errno={errno:?})")]
        Io { operation: &'static str, kind: std::io::ErrorKind, errno: Option<i32>, message: String },
        #[error("JSON decode: {0}")]
        Decode(String),
        #[error("schema validation: {0}")]
        Schema(String),
        #[error("operation denied: {0:?}")]
        Denied(JsonValue),
        #[error("call completion is uncertain; do not retry automatically: {0}")]
        Ambiguous(String),
        #[error("route unavailable: {0}")]
        Unavailable(String),
    }
    impl NodeError {
        pub fn decode(error: serde_json::Error) -> Self { Self::Decode(error.to_string()) }
        fn io(operation: &'static str, error: std::io::Error) -> Self {
            Self::Io { operation, kind:error.kind(), errno:error.raw_os_error(), message:error.to_string() }
        }
        fn backing(operation: &'static str, error: anyhow::Error) -> Self {
            if let Some(io) = error.downcast_ref::<std::io::Error>() {
                return Self::Io { operation, kind:io.kind(), errno:io.raw_os_error(), message:error.to_string() };
            }
            Self::Contract(format!("{operation}: {error:#}"))
        }
    }
    fn ensure(condition: bool, message: impl Into<String>) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        if condition { Ok(()) } else { Err(NodeError::Contract(message.into())) }
    }
    pub fn validate_identifier(value:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{
        ensure(!value.is_empty() && value.len()<=128 && !value.contains('\0'), "identifier must be nonempty, <=128 bytes, and contain no NUL (binding restriction)")
    }
    pub fn validate_hash(value:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{
        ensure(value.len()==64 && value.bytes().all(|b|b.is_ascii_hexdigit()),"hash must be 64 ASCII hexadecimal characters")
    }
    pub fn validate_store_name(value:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{
        ensure(!value.is_empty() && value.len()<=128 && value!="." && value!=".." && value.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"._-".contains(&b)),"invalid store name")
    }
    pub fn validate_pointer(value:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{
        ensure(value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('/'), "JSON pointer must be empty or begin with /")?;
        for part in value.split('/') {
            let mut chars=part.chars();
            while let Some(c)=chars.next(){ if c=='~' { ensure(matches!(chars.next(),Some('0'|'1')),"invalid JSON pointer escape (binding restriction)")?; } }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn validate_root(value:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{
        ensure(value.starts_with('/') && !value.contains('\0') && Path::new(value).components().all(|c| matches!(c,std::path::Component::RootDir|std::path::Component::Normal(_))),"root must be an absolute path without traversal (binding restriction)")
    }

    struct Mount {
        path:PathBuf, root:File, mount_id:String, metadata:serde_json::Value,
        view:ViewManifest, workspace:bool, calls:Option<MountedNamespace>,
    }
    impl Mount {
        fn open(path:&Path, session:Option<&str>, workspace:Option<&str>)->Result<Self,NodeError>{
            let path=std::fs::canonicalize(path).map_err(|e|NodeError::io("canonicalize mount",e))?;
            let root=OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY|libc::O_NOFOLLOW|libc::O_CLOEXEC).open(&path).map_err(|e|NodeError::io("open mount",e))?;
            let mount_id=fd_mount_id(&root)?;
            verify_fuse(&mount_id,&path)?;
            let metadata=read_json(open_relative(&root,".3tchedfs.json",false)?)?;
            let view:ViewManifest=serde_json::from_value(read_json(open_relative(&root,"view.json",false)?)?).map_err(NodeError::decode)?;
            ensure(metadata["format"]=="3tchedfs/1", "unsupported mount format")?;
            for key in ["format","view_id","source_catalog_hash","source_catalog_generation"] {
                ensure(metadata[key]==serde_json::to_value(&view).map_err(NodeError::decode)?[key],format!("mount/view {key} mismatch"))?;
            }
            ensure(metadata["object_count"].as_u64()==Some(view.objects.len() as u64),"mount catalog count mismatch")?;
            let is_workspace=workspace.is_some();
            if let Some(id)=workspace {
                ensure(metadata["workspace_id"].as_str()==Some(id),"workspace declaration mismatch")?;
            } else {
                ensure(metadata["workspace_id"].is_null(),"live mount must be an identity view")?;
                ensure(session.is_some() && metadata["session_id"].as_str()==session,"identity session mismatch")?;
            }
            let calls=if is_workspace {None} else {Some(MountedNamespace::open(&path,session).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("pin mounted calls",e))?)};
            let mount=Self {path,root,mount_id,metadata,view,workspace:is_workspace,calls};
            mount.verify()?;
            Ok(mount)
        }
        fn verify(&self)->Result<(),NodeError>{
            ensure(fd_mount_id(&self.root)?==self.mount_id,"pinned mount FD changed")?;
            verify_fuse(&self.mount_id,&self.path)?;
            let current=OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY|libc::O_NOFOLLOW).open(&self.path).map_err(|e|NodeError::io("verify mount root",e))?;
            let original=self.root.metadata().map_err(|e|NodeError::io("pinned root metadata",e))?;
            let present=current.metadata().map_err(|e|NodeError::io("current root metadata",e))?;
            ensure(fd_mount_id(&current)?==self.mount_id && original.dev()==present.dev() && original.ino()==present.ino(),"mount instance replaced")?;
            ensure(read_json(open_relative(&self.root,".3tchedfs.json",false)?)?==self.metadata,"mount identity/catalog declaration changed")?;
            ensure(read_json(open_relative(&self.root,"view.json",false)?)?==serde_json::to_value(&self.view).map_err(NodeError::decode)?,"pinned view changed")?;
            if let Some(calls)=&self.calls {calls.verify().map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("verify call context",e))?;}
            Ok(())
        }
        fn read(&self,key:&str)->Result<Vec<u8>,NodeError>{
            self.verify()?;
            let result=read_bounded(open_relative(&self.root,key,false)?,MAX_DOCUMENT);
            self.verify()?;
            result
        }
    }

    /// Factories pin a mode and locator. No route fallback occurs after a denial or missing node.

        pub fn direct_blob(store:ObjectStore, view:ViewId)->Result<Self,NodeError>{

            let namespace=Namespace::build(&store,ProjectionTarget::View(view.view_id.clone()),None).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("build frozen namespace",e))?;
            let mut inventory=BTreeMap::new();
            for node in namespace.nodes.values(){
                let key=node.path.trim_start_matches('/').to_owned();
                let kind=match node.kind {NodeKind::Directory=>HandleKind::Directory, NodeKind::Symlink(_)=>HandleKind::Symlink, _=> classify(&key,false,false)};
                let target=match &node.kind {NodeKind::Symlink(value)=>Some(value.clone()), _=>None};
                let mut desc=descriptor(key,kind)?;desc.target=target;inventory.insert(desc.key.clone(),desc);
            }
            Ok(Self::new(Backend::Direct {store,namespace,view},inventory))
        }
        pub fn via_fuse(root:MountRoot,session:SessionId)->Result<Self,NodeError>{

        }

        }

    pub struct NodeHandle { context:Arc<Context>, desc:Descriptor }
    impl NodeHandle {
        pub fn kind(&self)->HandleKind {self.desc.kind}
        pub fn require_route(&self,route:&str)->Result<(),NodeError>{

        }
        fn verify(&self)->Result<(),NodeError>{match &self.context.backend {Backend::Direct{store,view,..}=>{store.read_view(&view.view_id).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("verify frozen view",e))?;Ok(())},Backend::Fuse(mount)=>mount.verify()}}

                Backend::Fuse(mount)=>mount.read(&self.desc.key),
                Backend::Direct{namespace,..}=>{
                    let node=namespace.nodes.values().find(|n|n.path.trim_start_matches('/')==self.desc.key).ok_or_else(||NodeError::Contract("node no longer in frozen namespace".into()))?;
                    if let NodeKind::File(bytes)=&node.kind {Ok(bytes.read().clone())} else {Err(NodeError::Contract("node does not have a byte payload".into()))}
                }
            }

        pub fn list(&self)->Result<Vec<DirectoryEntry>,NodeError>{

            Ok(self.context.inventory.values().filter(|d| !d.key.is_empty() && d.parent==self.desc.key).map(|d| DirectoryEntry {name:d.name.clone(),kind:d.kind,owner:self.context.owner,key:d.key.clone()}).collect())
        }
        fn object(&self)->Result<TypedObject,NodeError>{
            let plugin=self.desc.plugin.as_deref().ok_or_else(||NodeError::Contract("node has no plugin locator".into()))?;
            match &self.context.backend {
                Backend::Direct{store,view,..}=>store.object_for_view(view,plugin).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("read pinned object",e)),
                Backend::Fuse(mount)=>{
                    if let Some(calls)=&mount.calls {calls.object(plugin).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("read mounted object",e))}
                    else {serde_json::from_slice(&mount.read(&format!("plugins/{}/object.blob.json",encode_component(plugin)))?).map_err(NodeError::decode)}

            }

        pub fn static_payload(&self)->Result<StaticPayload,NodeError>{
            ensure(self.kind()==HandleKind::StaticJson,"expected static JSON node")?;
            self.verify()?;
            let value:serde_json::Value=serde_json::from_slice(&self.bytes()?).map_err(NodeError::decode)?;
            macro_rules! decode {($variant:ident,$ty:ty)=>{Ok(StaticPayload::$variant(serde_json::from_value::<$ty>(value).map_err(NodeError::decode)?))};}
            match self.desc.name.as_str(){
                ".3tchedfs.json"=>decode!(MountMetadata,MountMetadata),"view.json"=>decode!(View,ViewManifest),"workspace.json"=>decode!(Workspace,Workspace),
                "object.blob.json"=>Ok(StaticPayload::Object(self.object()?)),"schema.json"=>Ok(StaticPayload::Schema(self.object()?.schema)),
                "capabilities.json"=>decode!(Capabilities,Capabilities),"input.schema.json"=>Ok(StaticPayload::Arguments(JsonValue::from_json(value)?)),
                "output.schema.json"=>Ok(StaticPayload::Returns(JsonValue::from_json(value)?)),"metadata.json"=>decode!(MethodMetadata,MethodDecl),
                _=>Err(NodeError::Contract("unclassified static payload".into()))
            }
        }
        pub fn object_hash(&self)->Result<ObjectHash,NodeError>{
            ensure(self.kind()==HandleKind::ObjectHashFile,"expected hash node")?;
            let bytes=self.bytes()?;let text=std::str::from_utf8(&bytes).map_err(|e|NodeError::Decode(e.to_string()))?;
            let hash=ObjectHash::new(text.trim())?;
            let plugin=self.desc.plugin.as_deref().ok_or_else(||NodeError::Contract("missing hash plugin".into()))?;
            match &self.context.backend {
                Backend::Direct{store,view,..}=>{
                    ensure(view.objects.get(plugin).map(String::as_str)==Some(hash.as_str()),"pinned object hash mismatch")?;
                    store.read_object(hash.as_str()).map_err(|e|NodeError::backing("verify hash object",e))?;
                },
                Backend::Fuse(mount) if !mount.workspace=>{
                    ensure(mount.view.objects.get(plugin).map(String::as_str)==Some(hash.as_str()),"mounted object hash differs from pinned view")?;
                },
                Backend::Fuse(_)=>{ /* Workspace object hashes may differ from their immutable base view. */ }
            }
            Ok(hash)
        }

            let Backend::Fuse(mount)=&self.context.backend else {return Err(NodeError::Unavailable("workspace write only through mounted workspace".into()));};
            ensure(mount.workspace,"write requires workspace mode")?;
            let _guard=self.context.gate.lock().map_err(|_|NodeError::Contract("factory operation lock poisoned".into()))?;
            mount.verify()?;
            validate_json_tree(&value,0,&mut 0)?;
            let bytes=serde_json::to_vec(&value).map_err(NodeError::decode)?;
            ensure(bytes.len()<=1024*1024,"workspace JSON exceeds binding 1 MiB bound")?;
            let mut file=open_relative(&mount.root,&self.desc.key,true)?;
            file.write_all(&bytes).map_err(|e|NodeError::Ambiguous(format!("partial workspace write: {e}")))?;

            file.sync_all().map_err(|e|NodeError::Ambiguous(format!("workspace fsync: {e}")))?;

            let value:serde_json::Value=serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(NodeError::decode)?;

    fn inspect(filesystem:&TypedFilesystem,directory:Directory,counts:&mut BTreeMap<&'static str,usize>)->Result<()> {

                TypedNode::StaticJson(node)=>{node.get()?;*counts.entry("static-json").or_default()+=1;},
                TypedNode::ObjectHashFile(node)=>{node.get()?;*counts.entry("object-hash").or_default()+=1;},

    fn formatted(source:&str)->Result<String>{
        let mut child=Command::new("rustfmt").args(["--edition","2024","--emit","stdout"]).stdin(Stdio::piped()).stdout(Stdio::piped()).stderr(Stdio::piped()).spawn().context("rustfmt is required for deterministic generated output")?;
        child.stdin.take().context("rustfmt stdin")?.write_all(source.as_bytes())?;
        let result=child.wait_with_output()?;
        ensure!(result.status.success(),"rustfmt failed: {}",String::from_utf8_lossy(&result.stderr));
        String::from_utf8(result.stdout).context("rustfmt output is not UTF-8")
    }
    fn main()->Result<()> {
        let mut args=std::env::args().skip(1);
        let input=PathBuf::from(args.next().unwrap_or_else(||"crates/threetched-fs/docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json".into()));
        let output=PathBuf::from(args.next().unwrap_or_else(||"crates/threetched-fs/src/typed_bindings.rs".into()));
        let check=args.next().as_deref()==Some("--check");
        ensure!(args.next().is_none(),"usage: typed_generate [schema] [output] [--check]");
        let schema:Value=serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&input)?)?;
        let source=formatted(&generate(&schema)?)?;
        if check {ensure!(std::fs::read_to_string(&output)?==source,"generated bindings differ; regenerate from {}",input.display());}
        else {std::fs::write(&output,source)?;}
        println!("{} {}",if check {"verified"} else {"generated"},output.display());
        Ok(())
    }

    //! Validate the self-contained filesystem contract and all source references.
    use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
    use std::path::Path;
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, ensure};
    use serde_json::Value;
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    
    fn visit(value: &Value, visitor: &mut impl FnMut(&str, &Value) -> Result<()>) -> Result<()> {
        match value {
            Value::Object(object) => {
                for (key, value) in object {
                    visitor(key, value)?;
                    visit(value, visitor)?;
                }
            }
            Value::Array(values) => {
                for value in values {
                    visit(value, visitor)?;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<()> {
        let path = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| {
            "crates/threetched-fs/docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json".to_owned()
        });
        let schema: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&path)?)?;
        jsonschema::draft202012::meta::validate(&schema)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid JSON Schema 2020-12: {error}"))?;
        let validator = jsonschema::Validator::new(&schema)?;
        validator
            .validate(&schema)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("contract does not match its structural schema: {error}"))?;
    
        let types = schema["types"].as_object().context("types")?;
        let names: BTreeSet<_> = types.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        let type_names = regex::Regex::new("[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*")?;
        let check_type = |name: &str| -> Result<()> {
            for token in type_names.find_iter(name).map(|m| m.as_str()) {
                ensure!(
                    names.contains(token)
                        || names.contains(format!("{token}<T>").as_str())
                        || ["Vec", "Option", "String", "bool", "u64", "usize"].contains(&token),
                    "undefined type {token} in {name}"
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        };
        let classes = schema["bindings"]["classes"].as_object().context("classes")?;
        let invariants: BTreeSet<_> = schema["invariants"]["required"]
            .as_array()
            .context("invariants")?
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|value| value["id"].as_str())
            .collect();
        let mut node_ids = BTreeSet::new();
        for node in schema["nodes"].as_array().context("nodes")? {
            ensure!(node_ids.insert(node["id"].as_str()), "duplicate node ID");
            ensure!(
                classes.contains_key(node["class"].as_str().context("class")?),
                "node class has no generated trait"
            );
            for param in node["params"].as_array().context("params")? {
                check_type(param["type"].as_str().context("param type")?)?;
            }
            check_type(node["backing"]["payload_type"].as_str().context("payload")?)?;
        }
        let mut method_ids = BTreeSet::new();
        for method in schema["methods"].as_array().context("methods")? {
            ensure!(method_ids.insert(method["id"].as_str()), "duplicate method ID");
            check_type(method["returns"].as_str().context("return")?)?;
            check_type(method["errors"].as_str().context("errors")?)?;
            for param in method["params"].as_array().context("method params")? {
                check_type(param["type"].as_str().context("method param type")?)?;
            }
            let class = &classes[method["receiver"].as_str().context("receiver")?];
            let declaration = class["operations"]
                .as_array()
                .context("operations")?
                .iter()
                .find(|op| op["name"] == method["name"])
                .context("method absent from generator class")?;
            ensure!(
                declaration["args"] == method["params"]
                    && declaration["return"] == method["returns"]
                    && declaration["receiver"] == method["borrow"],
                "method and generator signature disagree: {}",
                method["id"]
            );
            ensure!(
                class["routes"]
                    .as_array()
                    .context("routes")?
                    .contains(&method["route"]),
                "method route has no generated implementation"
            );
            for stage in ["pre", "post"] {
                for id in method["required_steps"][stage].as_array().context("steps")? {
                    ensure!(invariants.contains(id.as_str().context("step")?), "unknown invariant");
                }
            }
        }
    
        let citation = regex::Regex::new(r"^(.+):([0-9]+)(?:-([0-9]+))?$")?;
        let mut citations = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut line_counts = BTreeMap::new();
        visit(&schema, &mut |key, value| {
            if key == "$ref" {
                let reference = value.as_str().context("$ref is not a string")?;
                if let Some(pointer) = reference.strip_prefix('#') {
                    ensure!(schema.pointer(pointer).is_some(), "unresolved {reference}");
                }
            }
            if ["source_refs", "sources", "evidence", "x-source-refs"].contains(&key)
                && let Some(values) = value.as_array()
            {
                for source in values.iter().filter_map(Value::as_str) {
                    let Some(parts) = citation.captures(source) else { continue };
                    let file = parts[1].to_owned();
                    if !Path::new(&file).is_file() { continue }
                    let count = *line_counts.entry(file.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {
                        std::fs::read_to_string(&file).map(|s| s.lines().count()).unwrap_or(0)
                    });
                    let start: usize = parts[2].parse()?;
                    let end: usize = parts.get(3).map_or(Ok(start), |m| m.as_str().parse())?;
                    ensure!(start > 0 && start <= end && end <= count, "out-of-bounds source {source}");
                    citations.insert(source.to_owned());
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        for source in schema["versioning"]["source_files"].as_array().context("source hashes")? {
            let path = source["path"].as_str().context("source path")?;
            let actual = format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(std::fs::read(path)?));
            ensure!(source["sha256"] == actual, "source changed since schema assembly: {path}");
        }
        println!("JSON Schema 2020-12 + self-contract valid; {} types, {} nodes, {} methods, {} source citations; source digests match", types.len(), node_ids.len(), method_ids.len(), citations.len());
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn validate_session(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(
            !value.is_empty()
                && value.len() <= 128
                && value
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_'),
            "invalid lungs session selector",
        )

    pub fn validate_plugin(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(

                && value.len() <= 128
                && value

            "invalid canonical captured plugin id",
        )
    }
    pub fn validate_schema_hash(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(
            value.len() == 64
                && value
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(b, b'a'..=b'f')),
            "schema hash must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters",
        )

    pub fn validate_hash(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(

        )
    }
    pub fn validate_store_name(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(
            !value.is_empty()
                && value.len() <= 128
                && value != "."
                && value != ".."
                && value
                    .bytes()
                    .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"._-".contains(&b)),
            "invalid store name",
        )
    }
    pub fn validate_pointer(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(
            value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('/'),
            "JSON pointer must be empty or begin with /",
        )?;
        for part in value.split('/') {
            let mut chars = part.chars();
            while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
                if c == '~' {
                    ensure(
                        matches!(chars.next(), Some('0' | '1')),
                        "invalid JSON pointer escape (binding restriction)",
                    )?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn validate_root(value: &str) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
        ensure(
            value.starts_with('/')
                && !value.contains('\0')
                && Path::new(value).components().all(|c| {
                    matches!(
                        c,
                        std::path::Component::RootDir | std::path::Component::Normal(_)
                    )
                }),
            "root must be an absolute path without traversal (binding restriction)",
        )
    }

## User

if we put a cache  in shm  for this wold that be like a l3 cache?

## Assistant

Yes—as a **third software cache layer**, if we define:

- L1: snapshots held by open handles.
- L2: a per-mount cache of decoded or rendered values.
- L3: a shared cache across mounts in SHM.

It would still live in RAM; the CPU’s hardware L3 is separate. Since the backing files already live in SHM, caching another copy of their raw bytes offers little benefit. The useful shared cache would avoid repeated decoding/rendering, with keys that include committed generation, schema hash, and identity scope. I’ll include that option in the memory strategy, gated on measurements.

       311        /// Read a plugin's live state from SHM and extract the value at the given
       312        /// JSON pointer, as pretty-printed JSON bytes. Rendering happens once per
       313        /// committed state version; later opens and size checks reuse it.
       314        fn live_state_bytes(&self, node: &Node) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
       315            let (plugin_id, pointer) = match &node.kind {
       316                NodeKind::LiveFile { plugin_id, pointer } => (plugin_id.as_str(), pointer.as_str()),
       317                _ => return None,
       318            };
       319            let state_dir = self.namespace.state_dir.as_ref()?;
       320            let path = state_dir.join(format!("{plugin_id}.json"));
       321            let key = StateKey::of(&std::fs::metadata(&path).ok()?);
       322            let cache_key = (plugin_id.to_string(), pointer.to_string());
       323            if let Some((cached, bytes)) = self.live_cache.lock().get(&cache_key)
       324                && *cached == key
       325            {
       326                return Some(bytes.clone());
       327            }
       328            let raw = std::fs::read(&path).ok()?;
       329            let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).ok()?;
       330            let extracted = if pointer.is_empty() {
       331                value
       332            } else {
       333                value.pointer(pointer).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)
       334            };
       335            let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&extracted).ok()?;
       336            bytes.push(b'\n');
       337            // A commit that lands between the stat and the read is stored under
       338            // the older key, so the next open simply renders it again.
       339            self.live_cache
       340                .lock()
       341                .insert(cache_key, (key, bytes.clone()));
       342            Some(bytes)
       343        }

    #!/bin/sh
    # Assemble the reviewable source contract. Cargo generation/verification is
    # deliberately separate so the repository's execution worker runs it.
    set -eu
    cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."
    docs=crates/threetched-fs/docs
    source_list=$(mktemp)
    hash_list=$(mktemp)
    contract_tmp=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f "$source_list" "$hash_list" "$contract_tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
    
    jq -s -r '
      [.[] | .. | objects | (.source_refs?, .sources?, .evidence?, .["x-source-refs"]?)
        | arrays | .[] | strings
        | select(test("^(crates/|deploy/|/home/jeremy/.cargo/registry/)[^ ]+:[0-9]+"))
        | sub(":[0-9]+.*$"; "")]
      | unique[]
    ' "$docs/typed-filesystem-nodes.evidence.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-backing.evidence.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-binding-input.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-gaps.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-policy.json" > "$source_list"
    
    while IFS= read -r source_path; do
      sha256sum -- "$source_path"
    done < "$source_list" > "$hash_list"
    
    jq -Rn --arg commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
      '{source_files:[inputs|capture("^(?<sha256>[0-9a-f]{64})  (?<path>.*)$")],
        source_hash_algorithm:"SHA-256", assembly_commit:$commit}' \
      "$hash_list" > "$docs/typed-filesystem-provenance.json"
    
    jq -n -L "$docs" \
      --slurpfile nodes "$docs/typed-filesystem-nodes.evidence.json" \
      --slurpfile backing "$docs/typed-filesystem-backing.evidence.json" \
      --slurpfile binding "$docs/typed-filesystem-binding-input.json" \
      --slurpfile gaps "$docs/typed-filesystem-gaps.json" \
      --slurpfile provenance "$docs/typed-filesystem-provenance.json" \
      --slurpfile policy "$docs/typed-filesystem-policy.json" \
      -f "$docs/typed-filesystem-assemble.jq" > "$contract_tmp"
    mv "$contract_tmp" "$docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json"
    
    printf '%s\n' 'Assembled docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json; run typed_generate and typed_validate through the Cargo worker.'

    ---
    name: ovs-db-analysis
    description: >-
      Analyze Open vSwitch data from sosreport — conf.db, OpenFlow dumps, port stats,
      tunnels, and datapath health. Use when troubleshooting OVS packet drops, flow
      performance, bridge/port/interface issues, DPDK vs kernel datapath, or when the
      user mentions sosreport openvswitch, ovs-ofctl, ovsdb-tool, or ovs-db-analysis.
    ---
    
    # OVS Database and Flow Analysis
    
    This skill provides detailed analysis of Open vSwitch (OVS) data collected via sosreport. It operates in four modes:
    
    1. **Default mode**: Full analysis - conf.db + all text files (requires ovsdb-tool, falls back to text files if not available)
    2. **Database mode (`--db`)**: Database only - analyze conf.db (requires ovsdb-tool)
    3. **Text files mode (`--flows-only`)**: Text files only - no ovsdb-tool needed
    4. **Query mode (`--query`)**: Run custom OVSDB JSON queries (requires ovsdb-tool)
    
    ## When to Use This Skill
    
    Use this skill when:
    - **Troubleshooting packet drops** - Find drop flows being hit
    - **Analyzing flow performance** - View top flows by packet count
    - Analyzing OVS configuration from a sosreport
    - Troubleshooting bridge, port, or interface issues
    - Investigating DPDK vs kernelspace datapath
    - Reviewing tunnel configurations (VXLAN, Geneve, GRE)
    - Checking port statistics (drops, errors, traffic)
    - Mapping Kubernetes pods to OVS interfaces
    
    ## Prerequisites
    
    **Default mode** (full analysis):
    - **ovsdb-tool** must be installed (from openvswitch package)
    - Falls back to `--flows-only` if ovsdb-tool not found
    - Sosreport with `sos_commands/openvswitch/` directory and `conf.db`
    
    **Database mode** (`--db`):
    - **ovsdb-tool** must be installed (from openvswitch package)
      - Check: `which ovsdb-tool`
      - Fedora/RHEL: `sudo dnf install openvswitch`
      - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install openvswitch-common`
    - Sosreport with `conf.db` file
    
    **Text files mode** (`--flows-only`):
    - No special tools needed - works out of the box!
    - Sosreport with `sos_commands/openvswitch/` directory
    
    **Query mode** (`--query`):
    - **ovsdb-tool** must be installed
    - Incompatible with `--flows-only`
    
    ## File Locations in Sosreport
    
    The sosreport collects:
    ```
    sosreport-hostname-date/
    ├── etc/openvswitch/conf.db              (OVS database - for --db mode)
    ├── var/lib/openvswitch/conf.db          (alternate location)
    └── sos_commands/openvswitch/            (default mode uses these)
        ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_show              (topology)
        ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_bridge       (bridge details)
        ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_interface    (interface details)
        ├── ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_Open_vSwitch (system info)
        ├── ovs-ofctl_dump-flows_<bridge>    (OpenFlow entries)
        ├── ovs-ofctl_dump-ports_<bridge>    (Port statistics)
        ├── ovs-appctl_coverage.show         (internal stats)
        ├── ovs-appctl_upcall.show           (datapath health)
        ├── ovs-appctl_tnl.ports.show_-v     (tunnel ports)
        └── ...
    ```
    
    ## Analysis Script
    
    The analysis script is located at:
    ```
    <plugin-root>/skills/ovs-db-analysis/scripts/analyze_ovs_db.py
    ```
    
    ## Implementation Steps
    
    ### Step 1: Locate the Analysis Script
    
    ```bash
    SCRIPT_PATH=$(find ~ -name "analyze_ovs_db.py" -path "*/sosreport/skills/ovs-db-analysis/scripts/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    
    if [ -z "$SCRIPT_PATH" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: analyze_ovs_db.py script not found."
        exit 1
    fi
    ```
    
    ### Step 2: Run the Analysis
    
    ```bash
    # Default: Full analysis - conf.db + text files (requires ovsdb-tool)
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport-hostname-date/
    
    # Analyze from archive
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport-hostname-date.tar.xz
    
    # Database only mode (requires ovsdb-tool)
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --db
    
    # Text files only mode (no ovsdb-tool needed)
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --flows-only
    ```
    
    ### Step 3: Custom Queries (Optional, requires --db)
    
    For specific investigations, use raw OVSDB queries:
    
    ```bash
    # Query all bridges
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Bridge", "where":[], "columns":["name","datapath_type","fail_mode"]}]'
    
    # Query VXLAN interfaces
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Interface", "where":[["type","==","vxlan"]], "columns":["name","options"]}]'
    
    # Query interfaces with errors
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Interface", "where":[], "columns":["name","error"]}]'
    ```
    
    ## Analysis Output
    
    The default mode analyzes:
    
    | Analysis | Source File | Description |
    |----------|-------------|-------------|
    | System Info | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_Open_vSwitch` | OVS/DPDK version, system type, external IDs |
    | Topology | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_show` | Bridge overview with ports grouped by type |
    | Bridge Details | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_bridge` | Datapath type, fail mode, CT zones |
    | Interfaces | `ovs-vsctl_-t_5_list_interface` | By type, pod interfaces with mapping |
    | OpenFlow | `ovs-ofctl_dump-flows_*` | Flow counts, drops, top flows |
    | Port Stats | `ovs-ofctl_dump-ports_*` | RX/TX drops and errors |
    | Tunnels | `ovs-appctl_tnl.ports.show_-v` | Configured tunnel ports |
    | Datapath Health | `ovs-appctl_upcall.show` | Flow table usage vs limit |
    | OVS Stats | `ovs-appctl_coverage.show` | Internal counters (netlink, OVSDB, etc.) |
    
    ## OpenFlow Analysis Features
    
    | Feature | Description |
    |---------|-------------|
    | Flow Count | Total flows per bridge (total, drop, with hits) |
    | Drop Detection | Flows with `actions=drop` that have packet hits |
    | Top Flows | Most active flows sorted by n_packets |
    | Table Distribution | Flow counts per OpenFlow table |
    | Port Drops | RX/TX drop counters per port |
    | Port Errors | RX/TX error counters per port |
    | Datapath Health | Flow table usage vs limit (from upcall.show) |
    | OVS Stats | Internal statistics (netlink, OpenFlow, OVSDB transactions) |
    
    ## OVN Internal Tables (Ignore Drops in These)
    
    When analyzing drop flows in OVN-managed bridges (br-int), **ignore drops in table 44 and tables 64-87** as these are internal OVN mechanics, not security policy or real packet drops.
    
    > **⚠️ Note:** OVN and OVS are complex systems and table mappings can change between releases. Always verify drop analysis against the specific OVN version in use. When in doubt, check the OVN source code for your release.
    
    | Table | Name | Purpose |
    |-------|------|---------|
    | **44** | **CHK_LB_OUTPUT** | **Loopback prevention - drops packets that would loop back (high volume, normal)** |
    | 64 | SAVE_INPORT | Save ingress port for later |
    | 65 | LOG_TO_PHY | Logical to physical mapping |
    | 66 | MAC_BINDING | MAC binding lookups |
    | 67 | MAC_LOOKUP | MAC address table lookups |
    | 68-69 | CHK_LB_HAIRPIN | Load balancer hairpin checks |
    | 70 | CT_SNAT_HAIRPIN | Conntrack SNAT hairpin |
    | 71-72 | GET/LOOKUP_FDB | FDB (forwarding DB) lookups |
    | 73-74 | CHK_IN_PORT_SEC | Ingress port security |
    | 75 | CHK_OUT_PORT_SEC | Egress port security |
    | 76-77 | ECMP_NH | ECMP next-hop handling |
    | 78 | CHK_LB_AFFINITY | Load balancer affinity |
    | **79** | **MAC_CACHE_USE** | **MAC cache miss (high volume, normal)** |
    | 80 | CT_ZONE_LOOKUP | Conntrack zone lookup |
    | 81-83 | CT_ORIG_*_LOAD | Conntrack original tuple loading |
    | 84 | FLOOD_REMOTE_CHASSIS | Remote chassis flooding |
    | 85 | CT_STATE_SAVE | Conntrack state save |
    | 86 | CT_ORIG_PROTO_LOAD | Conntrack protocol loading |
    | 87 | GET_REMOTE_FDB | Remote FDB lookup |
    
    **Relevant drop tables for troubleshooting:**
    - **Table 9**: Ingress ACLs - actual policy drops (look for `reg0=0x8000`)
    - **Table 0**: Initial classification drops
    - **Tables < 64**: Generally meaningful drops
    
    ## Common Analysis Scenarios
    
    ### 1. Troubleshooting Packet Drops
    
    ```bash
    # Quick analysis (default mode, no ovsdb-tool)
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/
    ```
    
    Look for:
    - **ACTIVE DROP FLOWS** section showing flows dropping packets
    - **PORT STATISTICS** showing ports with drops/errors
    
    ### 2. Checking DPDK Configuration
    
    ```bash
    # Default mode shows DPDK info from text files
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/
    
    # Or use database mode for custom queries
    python3 "$SCRIPT_PATH" /path/to/sosreport/ --query '["Open_vSwitch", {"op":"select", "table":"Open_vSwitch", "where":[], "columns":["dpdk_initialized","other_config"]}]'
    ```
    
    ### 3. Investigating Pod Connectivity
    
    The interface analysis shows pod-to-OVS mapping:
    - Interfaces with `external_ids` containing `iface-id`
    - Interface names ending with `_h` (veth host side)
    
    ### 4. Datapath Health Check
    
    The upcall stats show:
    ```
    DATAPATH FLOW TABLE HEALTH
      Current flows: 155 / 200,000 (0.1% used)
      Average: 156, Max seen: 215
      ✓ Flow table healthy
    ```
    
    If usage > 90%, flows are being evicted too aggressively.
    
    ## Output Example
    

    ## Error Handling
    
    | Error | Solution |
    |-------|----------|
    | `ovsdb-tool not found` | Install openvswitch package OR use default mode (no --db) |
    | `conf.db not found` | Use default mode (analyzes text files instead) |
    | `sos_commands/openvswitch not found` | Ensure sosreport has OVS data collected |
