    ## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants (read these before touching plugins, state, or identity)
    
    - **Identity storage lifecycle (owner correction 2026-10-05).** Cozo owns identity-to-leaf/loop assignment and isolation. One immutable physical seed is shared through read-only views; each identity keeps its own writable leaf and the existing seven subvolumes. Only the external host provisioner may add a new blank leaf once, during explicit creation. Login, start, stop, logout, restart, bridge recovery and failed-start cleanup must NEVER add/remove Btrfs members. Start verifies/remounts the existing pair through the host mount owner; stop leaves membership and data intact. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage and records logical attachment. Do not interpret `attached=false` as device removal. No root copies, snapshots, new subvolumes or OverlayFS fallback during identity provisioning. Never modify a seed while retained leaves depend on it. Older add-on-start/remove-on-stop guidance in source, handoffs and signals is superseded; do not restore it. Host release snapshot/send/receive below is a separate deployment mechanism.
    - **D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`. No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops in plugin/service code. New backend capabilities register as plugins in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs` — never as new gRPC proto service packages.
    - **The plugin IS the schema — one source of truth, nonnegotiable.** That single schema is sealed into the blob, which IS the plugin. D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from it. Validate inputs against it. Each plugin defines its schema under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, using `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`. **There must be no parallel plugin schema source in a repository-level or plugin `schemas/` directory.** The former plugin capture directories, separate section files, and JSON-file loader have been removed. `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_loader.rs` still exists by name, but it reads only a manifest-pinned `PluginSchema` from the sealed blob catalog; it is not a file-schema fallback. The tched_router upstream document is imported once into `tched_router_contract.rs`; `tched_router_config_surface.rs` and its methods derive from that plugin-owned contract. Importing a new binary schema must replace that embedded contract through `gen_tched_router_config_surface --import-json`; it must not create a second captured-schema authority. Older docs claiming a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` are also stale — that file does not exist. Owner reaffirmed this rule on 2026-09-13.
    - **The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`. A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob`. Consumers read SHM directly (zero-copy) — they never re-hash and never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder and `live-schema.json` are gone.
    - **MutationEngine owns state; streaming comes from SHM (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** MutationEngine folds authoritative backend results into the complete state tree, including child objects, and commits that state to canonical SHM before change notifications. Child updates/deletions must preserve unrelated children and parent fields. Existing subscriptions derive their values from committed SHM; an in-memory event payload, method argument, or generator buffer is not a second state authority. Preserve verified principal/session scope for private state. Do not add a separate per-method streaming control plane or claim a buffered unary response provides state streaming.
    - **MCP gateway (settled).** One public MCP door: `:8090` on `op-grpc-bridge` (cognitive MCP is in-process there; no standalone `op-cognitive-mcp` runit service). `compact_mcp` is a retired plugin id. Compact *mode* (4 meta-tools) is in-process in op-web for the singleton control-plane chatbot; it is not an MCP plugin and not a second listener. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.
    - **External binaries back plugins; the plugin remains the single schema source.** 3tched-router / tched-router (`tched_router` in code) is the framework/schema/plugin integration backed by the autonomous `/usr/bin/zeroclaw` executable. The reproducible native input is pinned in `vendor/tched-router/source.pin`; `vendor/tched-router/build-native.sh` applies the checked-in patches and emits `target/native-artifacts/tched-router/{zeroclaw,manifest.json}` without installing it. `build-golden.sh` validates the pin, patch and binary provenance, then stages the binary, manifest, `/etc/op-dbus/zeroclaw-runtime.toml`, and the tracked default skill bundle into the golden filesystem. The `tched-router` runit service verifies that manifest, exact commit, binary digest, and version before exec, then seeds its private runtime config and skills from those staged bootstrap files. A fresh checkout includes the digest-pinned upstream source archive, patches and build recipe; the helper verifies and uses that archive by default. Cargo registry dependencies and system build tools still need provisioning. The executable keeps its upstream name. The plugin contract remains `tched_router_contract.rs`, and source attribution may identify `zeroclaw config schema`.
    - **Owner-confirmed lifecycle and model roles (2026-09-13, reaffirmed 2026-09-14).** Waypipe is retired: its crate directory, Cargo membership, binary target and protocol are absent; `retired-binaries`/`retired-services` prevent stale build or service artifacts from entering golden. Do not restore it in source exports or release inputs. Assistant is the control-plane chatbot, not an `assistant` container. The historical Gemma routing role is model agnostic; the `op-gemma` crate is retired (2026-09-19: directory, Cargo membership and binary removed, listed in `retired-binaries`) — the `gemma_brain` plugin remains and its role does not constrain the model/provider. Cargo membership and legacy names do not establish active deployments.
    - **Factory role correction (2026-09-14).** The former Factory account/platform plugin is retired from the registry and dispatch. The intended access is CLI/SSH; routing belongs to `tched_router`, and Factory billing requires an actual native binding. Provider names or relabelled direct upstream routes do not prove that binding. A future Missions integration needs its own verified native contract; do not restore the retired REST platform methods from historical fixtures or docs.
    - **Standalone vendor adapters are retired (2026-09-14).** The `op-grpc-adapters` crate directory and its `op.adapters.v1` protocol are absent after Netmaker retirement. Its duplicate mail/MQ services bypassed canonical plugin admission. Do not restore this crate or its old Netmaker clients. The existing bridge `operation.mail.v1` service and retained EMQX plugin are separate surfaces; their presence does not prove every mail or MQTT method is implemented.
    - **Owner-confirmed network topology (2026-09-13).** There is no WireGuard on this server. WireGuard terminates at the decoy; identity is transported by WARP. WireGuard types, plugin declarations, credentials or historical configuration paths in source do not establish a server WireGuard interface or a requirement to install one. Classify those surfaces by their decoy/server role before proposing implementation or retirement. An unwired `wgcf` method is not evidence that the actual WARP identity transport is broken.
    - **Identity minting and metadata (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** The identity subsystem owns minting the identity and its SealedId/SID1 credential blob. This is distinct from an OPBLOB01 plugin blob and does not belong in the plugin catalog. Clients forward the authored credential through the transport's identity metadata; they do not mint or reconstruct it from genesis/trace/key headers. Verify minting, persistence, injection and receiver validation as separate links. Current source assigns session/SID1 creation to MutationEngine with the op-identity format; the existence of an HTTP/MCP helper does not prove every gRPC client injects SID1.
    - **Owner decisions: decoy GRE, TLS and identity injection (2026-09-25).** The owner directed these changes; do not restore the previous layout. The door stays `10.0.0.2:8090`: tonic with the internal `svc0` certificate from the op-dbus local CA. The bridge no longer listens on `127.0.0.1:8090` or `10.0.0.3:8090`, and it no longer serves a second browser certificate. Browser-facing TLS terminates on the decoy at `10.0.0.1`. The decoy mints the sealed identity blob, and WARP delivers it to the 8090 interceptor, which anchors the session and writes the identity metadata (`anchor_verified_human_session` and `insert_identity_metadata` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs`). The oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed proof of the WireGuard peer, because WireGuard exists only on the decoy; the human credential (SID1) is the session identity for that key. The bridge's own client and MutationEngine are the wrong place for session or identity injection. Source and live state do not match this yet (2026-09-25): the interceptor still mints genesis server-side when no session exists (`mint_and_store_genesis` in `anchor_verified_human_session`), the decoy issuer mints only OIA1, and the decoy routes browser traffic for `10.0.0.2` over `gre-host` with no WARP route in either main routing table. The `gre-decoy` tunnel joins decoy and host (`deploy/runit/gre-decoy`): outer `188.68.58.237` ↔ `129.80.64.127`, inner `192.168.255.1/30` plus `10.0.0.2/32`, with `10.0.0.1` and the WireGuard clients `10.0.0.5`–`10.0.0.7` routed via `192.168.255.2`. GRE routing replaces NAT on this path: nftables is the firewall only, never a router, so do not add DNAT, SNAT or masquerade for it. Filter rules such as accepting GRE from the decoy are fine. GRE is not encrypted, so anything crossing it that is not TLS is readable on the path. MQTT stays on `10.0.0.3`, aliased on `ovsbr0` beside the OpenFlow address `10.200.0.1`. Xray runs in its container. op-web's page address is `http://10.0.0.4:8080`: plain HTTP outside the TLS zone, with `10.0.0.4/32` on `gre-decoy` and routed from the decoy over `gre-host`. The decoy issuer (`/etc/systemd/system/op-decoy-issuer.service.d/browser-auth.conf` on the decoy, not in this repo) hands out the IP door `https://10.0.0.2:8090` and allows the `10.0.0.4` and `10.0.0.2` page origins; no domain name points browsers at the decoy. Still open on 2026-09-25: how the decoy-minted oracle reaches the interceptor. The owner's direction is that it travels over GRE; whether it rides inside the relayed request or separately is undecided. Until that lands, the deployed page still fetches OIA1 from `http://10.0.0.1:51888/identity/self`, and the door rejects a request that carries no credential.
    - **Btrfs storage and transport (owner correction 2026-09-23).** Deployment remains the prepared snapshot transferred by `btrfs send/receive`. The earlier global five-subvolume limit and instruction to replace Snowball/cache subvolumes with ordinary directories are withdrawn. Preserve the original `operation-dbus-proto` cache/NUMA/timing architecture: Btrfs cache category subvolumes; authoritative timing plus vector/state subvolumes; aligned read-only snapshot sets and send/receive. See the original repo `branding/product-baseline.md` §12 and `crates/op-snowball/{DESIGN,REQUIREMENTS}.md` (R5). Retention is configurable per storage owner, not a global five-subvolume cap. Parent snapshots do not include nested subvolume contents: snapshot and transport every required member explicitly. Never flatten existing subvolumes or delete historical data to satisfy the withdrawn limit. Preserve security, writer-locking, identity and error-handling fixes while correcting storage regressions.
    - **No SQLite — use CozoDB.** CozoDB (`op-cozo-store`) is the embedded database for this project. Do not add new `rusqlite` or other SQLite use. `op-cache/src/btrfs_cache.rs` already uses a Cozo index; current `workstack_cache.rs`, `workflow_cache.rs`, `workflow_tracker.rs`, and `pattern_tracker.rs` still use `rusqlite` and remain migration debt rather than an approved pattern.

Voyage-4 models are interchangeable across their dimension (1024 for all variants); `_large` and `_lite` refer to model size/quality tier, not embedding space. All collections share a single fused retrieval space and can be queried together. Legacy `repos_lsp_*_voyage_code_4` collections and `repomix_rag` collection are retired — do not use them.     ## Handoff between agents
    
    Claude, Codex, Grok and any other agent share one handoff: `HANDOFF.md`. Read it
    at the start of every session, after this file. Claim your task in its *Active
    work* table before changing anything, and never reset, stash or overwrite work
    another agent has claimed there. Before the session ends, or before a context or
    usage limit, update your row and add a dated *Handoff* entry. A handoff kept only
    in one agent's private memory is invisible to the others, so it does not count.
    
    ## Signals and task board
    
    - **Append observations to `SIGNALS.md`** rather than letting them evaporate in chat. Three signal types: `💡 SUGGESTION` · `⚠️ CONCERN` · `👁️ OBSERVATION`. Each row: date · model · signal · optional `→ OD-##` link. Models leave status `open`. Promote anything actionable to `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.

    - **Read recent `SIGNALS.md` rows before non-trivial work** in the area they touch — the file records load-bearing gotchas (stale vendored deps, live/deployed drift, the live-vs-intent identity topology) that source alone will not surface.

    ## Subagent and model selection
    
    **Owner preference (2026-09-13, model names withdrawn 2026-09-24,
    reaffirmed 2026-09-30): assess task
    difficulty and required reasoning before delegation, and use the cheapest
    available model that can complete it at the same quality.** A lower price must
    not thin the answer, skip evidence, or weaken a judgment. If the cheaper model
    would lose accuracy, completeness, or care, use the more capable model. Pick
    from the models the session can actually launch. Do not inherit an expensive
    parent model by default, and do not pin a product or model id in this file.
    Use a low-cost model for lookups, inventory extraction, documentation
    assembly, builds, tests, and routine checks when that model can match the
    quality of a more capable one. Choose low effort for mechanical work and
    medium effort for bounded reasoning. Escalate when the task's quality needs
    it or a cheaper attempt falls short, and briefly state why.
    
    Keep the primary agent available for user communication and coordination.
    Delegate longer execution and research jobs, use nonblocking progress checks,
    and avoid long blocking tool calls on the primary. User messages steer active
    work; answer them promptly while delegated work continues. Small immediate
    edits and decisions can remain with the primary when delegation would add
    overhead.
    
    Prefer the **least-expensive subagent whose output matches a more capable model** for builds and tests:
    
    - `Explore` (fast read-only) for locating code, grepping symbols, answering "where is X."
    - `Plan` for architecture and design before writing code.
    - `general-purpose` only when the task needs multi-step reasoning or execution that Explore or Plan cannot cover.
    - Use a more capable model for complex cross-crate reasoning, security review, or ambiguous architectural decisions, and for any standard edit, build fix, or test whose quality would drop on the low-cost agent.
    - Do not spawn a subagent for a single-file edit or a direct grep you can do yourself.

    //! 3tchedFS filesystem registration and its single, shared invocation convention.
    //!
    //! This describes the existing FUSE implementation, not a second method router.
    //! Target declarations and admission remain owned by each sealed plugin. Mount
    //! identity and live contents remain in the identity's own filesystem namespace.
    
    use anyhow::{Result, bail, ensure};
    use async_trait::async_trait;
    use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
    use op_state_store::{CapabilityDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;
    
    use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::method_decl_from_schemars_with_output;
    
    pub const PLUGIN_NAME: &str = "threetched_fs";
    const VERSION: &str = "1.0.0";
    const READ_PROTOCOL: &str = "cap.storage.3tchedfs.protocol.read@v1";
    
    /// One convention for every declared operation file, relative to the mount.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    pub struct Invocation {
        /// Percent-encoded path components; resolve against the pinned catalog.
        pub path: String,
        /// Open one descriptor without truncating, then retain it through the reply.
        pub open: String,
        pub arguments: String,
        pub commit: String,
        pub result: String,
        /// Target-owned declaration, including input/output schemas and capability.
        pub declaration: String,
        /// A transport error can leave execution uncertain; never replay implicitly.
        pub automatic_retry: bool,
    }
    
    /// Static filesystem contract. This never asserts that a mount is ready.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.storage.3tchedfs.schema@v1"))]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "storage"))]
    pub struct FilesystemProtocol {
        pub filesystem_type: String,
        /// Mount-local metadata holds the actual identity and pinned catalog.
        pub mount_metadata: String,
        pub invocation: Invocation,
    }
    
    impl Default for FilesystemProtocol {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                filesystem_type: "fuse.3tchedFS".into(),
                mount_metadata: ".3tchedfs.json".into(),
                invocation: Invocation {
                    path: "plugins/{plugin}/operations/{method}/call".into(),
                    open: "O_RDWR".into(),
                    arguments: "application/json".into(),
                    commit: "fsync".into(),
                    result: "seek(0), read receipt or diagnostic on the same descriptor".into(),
                    declaration: "plugins/{plugin}/operations/{method}/metadata.json".into(),
                    automatic_retry: false,
                },
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    pub struct GetProtocolInput {}
    
    #[derive(Default)]
    pub struct ThreeTchedFsPlugin;
    
    #[async_trait]
    impl StatePlugin for ThreeTchedFsPlugin {
        fn name(&self) -> &str {
            PLUGIN_NAME
        }
        fn version(&self) -> &str {
            VERSION
        }
        fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
            Some(threetched_fs_schema())
        }
    
        async fn calculate_diff(&self, current: &Value, desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
            ensure!(
                current == desired && *desired == protocol_value()?,
                "3tchedFS protocol is immutable"
            );
            Ok(StateDiff {
                plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.into(),
                actions: vec![],
                metadata: DiffMetadata {
                    timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                    current_hash: String::new(),
                    desired_hash: String::new(),
                },
            })
        }
        async fn apply_state(&self, diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
            ensure!(
                diff.plugin == PLUGIN_NAME && diff.actions.is_empty(),
                "3tchedFS protocol is immutable"
            );
            Ok(ApplyResult {
                success: true,
                changes_applied: vec![],
                errors: vec![],
                checkpoint: None,
            })
        }
        async fn verify_state(&self, desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
            Ok(*desired == protocol_value()?)
        }
        async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
            bail!("3tchedFS protocol has no mutable checkpoints")
        }
        async fn rollback(&self, _: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
            bail!("3tchedFS protocol has no mutable checkpoints")
        }
        fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
            PluginCapabilities {
                supports_rollback: false,
                supports_checkpoints: false,
                supports_verification: true,
                atomic_operations: true,
            }
        }
    }
    
    fn protocol_value() -> Result<Value> {
        Ok(simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(
            FilesystemProtocol::default(),
        )?)
    }
    
    pub fn threetched_fs_schema() -> PluginSchema {
        let root =
            serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(FilesystemProtocol)).expect("protocol schema");
        let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
            PLUGIN_NAME,
            VERSION,
            "Identity-bound 3tchedFS filesystem and shared operation-file invocation convention",
            &root,
        );
        schema.category = "storage".into();
        schema.display_name = Some("3tchedFS".into());
        schema.tags = vec!["immutable".into(), "filesystem".into()];
        schema.immutable_paths = vec![
            "/filesystem_type".into(),
            "/mount_metadata".into(),
            "/invocation".into(),
        ];
        // Only the public protocol is global. No session, file content, or mount
        // readiness is fabricated or copied into shared public state.
        schema.public_state.paths = schema.immutable_paths.clone();
        let state = protocol_value().expect("protocol serializes");
        super::schemars_adapter::apply_state_defaults(&mut schema, &state);
        schema.example = Some(state);
        schema.methods.insert(
            "get_protocol".into(),
            method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<GetProtocolInput, FilesystemProtocol>(
                "get_protocol",
                SideEffect::Read,
                true,
                READ_PROTOCOL,
                "obs.storage.3tchedfs.protocol.get@v1",
            ),
        );
        schema.capabilities.insert(
            READ_PROTOCOL.into(),
            CapabilityDecl {
                id: READ_PROTOCOL.into(),
                description:
                    "Read the shared 3tchedFS invocation convention; grants no target operation access."
                        .into(),
            },
        );
        schema
    }
    
    pub fn dispatch(method: &str, arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
        ensure!(
            method == "get_protocol",
            "unknown 3tchedFS method: {method}"
        );
        let _: GetProtocolInput = serde_json::from_value(arguments.clone())?;
        Ok(serde_json::to_value(FilesystemProtocol::default())?)
    }
    
    inventory::submit! {
        crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new(PLUGIN_NAME, |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(ThreeTchedFsPlugin))
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        #[test]
        fn sealed_filesystem_contract_preserves_protocol_and_target_authority() {
            let schema = threetched_fs_schema();
            assert!(schema.validate_capability_closure().missing.is_empty());
            for subid in schema
                .subids
                .values()
                .chain(schema.methods.values().map(|m| &m.subid))
            {
                super::super::common::oscal::validate_subid(subid).unwrap();
            }
            let blob = op_blob::blobify_plugin_schema(PLUGIN_NAME, schema);
            assert_eq!(
                blob.manifest.dbus.object_path,
                crate::canonical::plugin_path(PLUGIN_NAME)
            );
            assert_eq!(
                blob.manifest.dbus.object_path,
                format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{PLUGIN_NAME}")
            );
            let bytes = blob.seal();
            let pinned =
                op_blob::BlobRef::from_manifest_pinned(&bytes, &blob.manifest.schema_hash).unwrap();
            let sealed = pinned.state_store_schema().unwrap();
            let protocol = protocol_value().unwrap();
            assert!(sealed.validate(&protocol).valid);
            assert!(sealed.capability_grants.is_empty());
            assert!(sealed.field_writes.is_empty());
            let method = &sealed.methods["get_protocol"];
            let output_schema = serde_json::to_value(method.returns.as_ref().unwrap()).unwrap();
            let validator = jsonschema::validator_for(&output_schema).unwrap();
            assert!(validator.is_valid(&dispatch("get_protocol", &serde_json::json!({})).unwrap()));
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn registered_contract_has_an_executable_descriptor_and_no_target_proxy() {
            assert!(
                crate::default_registry::DefaultPluginRegistry::available_plugins()
                    .iter()
                    .any(|id| id == PLUGIN_NAME)
            );
            let schema = threetched_fs_schema();
            assert_eq!(schema.methods.len(), 1);
            let output = dispatch("get_protocol", &serde_json::json!({})).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                output,
                serde_json::to_value(schema.example.unwrap()).unwrap()
            );
            assert!(dispatch("invoke", &serde_json::json!({})).is_err());
            assert!(dispatch("get_protocol", &serde_json::json!({"session": "another"})).is_err());
        }
    
        #[tokio::test]
        async fn rejects_protocol_mutation_and_false_checkpoint_support() {
            let plugin = ThreeTchedFsPlugin;
            let state = protocol_value().unwrap();
            assert!(plugin.verify_state(&state).await.unwrap());
            assert!(
                plugin
                    .calculate_diff(&state, &simd_json::json!({}))
                    .await
                    .is_err()
            );
            assert!(plugin.create_checkpoint().await.is_err());
        }
    }

    #!/bin/sh
    # Assemble the reviewable source contract. Cargo generation/verification is
    # deliberately separate so the repository's execution worker runs it.
    set -eu
    cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."
    docs=crates/threetched-fs/docs
    source_list=$(mktemp)
    hash_list=$(mktemp)
    contract_tmp=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f "$source_list" "$hash_list" "$contract_tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
    
    jq -s -r '
      [.[] | .. | objects | (.source_refs?, .sources?, .evidence?, .["x-source-refs"]?)
        | arrays | .[] | strings
        | select(test("^(crates/|deploy/|/home/jeremy/.cargo/registry/)[^ ]+:[0-9]+"))
        | sub(":[0-9]+.*$"; "")]
      | unique[]
    ' "$docs/typed-filesystem-nodes.evidence.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-backing.evidence.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-binding-input.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-gaps.json" \
      "$docs/typed-filesystem-policy.json" > "$source_list"
    
    while IFS= read -r source_path; do
      sha256sum -- "$source_path"
    done < "$source_list" > "$hash_list"
    
    jq -Rn --arg commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
      '{source_files:[inputs|capture("^(?<sha256>[0-9a-f]{64})  (?<path>.*)$")],
        source_hash_algorithm:"SHA-256", assembly_commit:$commit}' \
      "$hash_list" > "$docs/typed-filesystem-provenance.json"
    
    jq -n -L "$docs" \
      --slurpfile nodes "$docs/typed-filesystem-nodes.evidence.json" \
      --slurpfile backing "$docs/typed-filesystem-backing.evidence.json" \
      --slurpfile binding "$docs/typed-filesystem-binding-input.json" \
      --slurpfile gaps "$docs/typed-filesystem-gaps.json" \
      --slurpfile provenance "$docs/typed-filesystem-provenance.json" \
      --slurpfile policy "$docs/typed-filesystem-policy.json" \
      --slurpfile verification "$docs/typed-filesystem-verification.json" \
      -f "$docs/typed-filesystem-assemble.jq" > "$contract_tmp"
    mv "$contract_tmp" "$docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json"
    
    printf '%s\n' 'Assembled docs/typed-filesystem.schema.json; run typed_generate and typed_validate through the Cargo worker.'
    # Source-derived filesystem contract, not a PluginSchema authoring surface.
    # Inputs: nodes, backing, binding, gaps, provenance (slurpfile arrays).
    include "typed-filesystem-payloads";
    def typed_params:
      map(. + {source_path_encoding:.type,type:(if .name=="dependency" then "DependencyId" elif .type=="EncodedPluginId" then "PluginId" elif .type=="EncodedMethodKey" then "MethodId" elif .type=="EncodedCapabilityId" then "CapabilityId" elif .type=="EncodedJsonObjectKey" then "FieldKey" elif (.type|startswith("ArrayIndex")) then "ArrayIndex" elif (.type|startswith("Vec<")) then "Vec<PathSegment>" else .type end)});
    def routes($class):
      if ["Directory","StaticJson","ObjectHashFile","FrozenValue","Symlink"] | index($class)
      then ["direct-blob","via-fuse"] else ["via-fuse"] end;
    def payload($id; $class):
      if $class == "Directory" then "Vec<DirectoryEntry>"
      elif $class == "Symlink" then "SemanticLocator"
      elif $class == "ObjectHashFile" then "ObjectHash"
      elif ["LiveValue","FrozenValue","WorkspaceField"] | index($class) then "JsonValue"
      else ({mount_metadata:"MountMetadata",view_manifest:"ViewManifest",workspace_manifest:"Workspace",typed_object:"TypedObject",plugin_schema:"PluginSchema",required_capabilities:"Capabilities",input_schema:"JsonSchema",output_schema:"JsonSchema",method_metadata:"MethodDecl",method_call:"CallReceipt",method_result:"CallReceipt",method_error:"OperationDiagnostic"}[$id] // "unverified") end;
    def backing_descriptor($n; $class):
      {kind:(if $class=="LiveValue" then "shm"
        elif ["FrozenValue","WorkspaceField"]|index($class) then "blob"
        elif ["typed_object","plugin_schema","required_capabilities","input_schema","output_schema","method_metadata","view_manifest"]|index($n.id) then "blob"
        else "synthetic" end),
       locator_template:(if $class=="LiveValue" then "{state_dir:StateDirectory}/{plugin:PluginId}.json#{pointer:JsonPointer}"
        elif ["FrozenValue","WorkspaceField"]|index($class) then "{store:StoreRoot}/objects/{object_hash:ObjectHash}.blob#/value{pointer:JsonPointer}"
        elif $n.id=="view_manifest" then "{store:StoreRoot}/views/{view_id:ViewId}.json"
        elif ["typed_object","plugin_schema","required_capabilities","input_schema","output_schema","method_metadata"]|index($n.id) then "{store:StoreRoot}/objects/{object_hash:ObjectHash}.blob"
        else null end),

    /// Materialize a deterministic initial live state from a plugin schema.
    ///
    /// This is the schema-side bootstrap for D-Bus projection creation. It never
    /// queries a plugin backend and never invents data outside the contract:
    /// field defaults win, then examples, then an empty value matching the field
    /// type. The MutationEngine writes this once when no projection exists yet;
    /// later mutations replace it through the normal `/dev/shm/opdbus/state`
    /// write door.
    pub(crate) fn materialize_state_from_schema(schema: &PluginSchema) -> Value {
        if let Some(example) = &schema.example {
            return example.clone();
        }
    
        let mut state = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
        let mut fields = schema.fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        fields.sort_by_key(|(a, _)| *a);
    
        for (name, field) in fields {
            state.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));
        }
    
        Value::Object(Box::new(state))
    }
    
    fn materialize_field(field: &FieldSchema) -> Value {
        if let Some(value) = &field.default {
            return value.clone();
        }
        if let Some(value) = &field.example {
            return value.clone();
        }
    
        materialize_field_type(&field.field_type)
    }
    
    fn materialize_field_type(field_type: &FieldType) -> Value {
        match field_type {
            FieldType::String => json!(""),
            FieldType::Integer => json!(0),
            FieldType::Float => json!(0.0),
            FieldType::Boolean => json!(false),
            FieldType::Array(_) => json!([]),
            FieldType::Object(fields) => {
                let mut object = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
                let mut fields = fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
                fields.sort_by_key(|(a, _)| *a);
                for (name, field) in fields {
                    object.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));
                }
                Value::Object(Box::new(object))
            }
            FieldType::Enum(values) => values
                .first()
                .map(|value| json!(value))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| json!(null)),
            FieldType::OneOf(types) => types
                .first()
                .map(materialize_field_type)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| json!(null)),
            FieldType::Map(_) => json!({}),
            FieldType::JsonSchema(_) | FieldType::Any => json!(null),
        }
    }

    fn references(node: &Value, out: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
        match node {
            Value::Object(map) => {
                if let Some(name) = map
                    .get("$ref")
                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
                    .and_then(|r| r.strip_prefix("#/$defs/"))
                {
                    out.insert(name.to_string());
                }
                for child in map.values() {
                    references(child, out);
                }
            }
            Value::Array(items) => {
                for child in items {
                    references(child, out);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    fn visit(value: &Value, visitor: &mut impl FnMut(&str, &Value) -> Result<()>) -> Result<()> {

            if character != '~' {
                output.push(character);
                continue;
            }
            match chars.next() {
                Some('0') => output.push('~'),
                Some('1') => output.push('/'),
                _ => {
                    return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                        "path {pointer:?} contains invalid RFC 6901 escaping"
                    )));
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(output)
    }

        pub(crate) async fn call_generated_plugin_method_typed<Req, Res>(
            &self,
            plugin_id: &'static str,
            method_name: &'static str,
            request_message_name: &'static str,
            response_message_name: &'static str,
            request: Request<Req>,
        ) -> Result<Response<Res>, Status>
        where
            Req: prost::Message + Default,
            Res: prost::Message + Default,
        {
            let human_identity = request
                .extensions()
                .get::<crate::oracle_assertion::HumanPrincipalIdentity>()
                .cloned();
            let identity = interceptor::bridge_capability_identity(request.extensions());
    
            let bound_oracle = request
                .extensions()
                .get::<crate::oracle_assertion::BoundOracleProof>()
                .cloned();
            let declared_capability = request
                .metadata()
                .get(DECLARED_CAPABILITY_HEADER)
                .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
                .map(str::trim)
                .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
                .map(str::to_string);
    
            let sealed_schema = read_plugin_schema_json(plugin_id);
            let sealed_schema = sealed_schema
                .as_ref()
                .ok_or_else(|| Status::failed_precondition("sealed method schema is unavailable"))?;
    
            let request_bytes = request.into_inner().encode_to_vec();
            let request_desc = plugin_descriptor_pool()
                .get_message_by_name(request_message_name)
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    Status::internal(format!(
                        "missing request descriptor for {plugin_id}.{method_name}"
                    ))
                })?;
            let request_dynamic = DynamicMessage::decode(request_desc, request_bytes.as_slice())
                .map_err(|error| {
                    Status::internal(format!(
                        "failed to decode typed request for {plugin_id}.{method_name}: {error}"
                    ))
                })?;
    
            let response_desc = plugin_descriptor_pool()
                .get_message_by_name(response_message_name)
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    Status::internal(format!(
                        "missing response descriptor for {plugin_id}.{method_name}"
                    ))
                })?;
    
            let response_dynamic = self
                .call_plugin_method_dynamic(
                    plugin_id,
                    method_name,
                    request_dynamic,
                    &response_desc,
                    sealed_schema,
                    identity.as_ref(),
                    human_identity.as_ref(),
                    declared_capability.as_deref(),
                    bound_oracle.clone(),
                )
                .await?;
    
            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
            response_dynamic.encode(&mut bytes).map_err(|error| {
                Status::internal(format!(
                    "failed to encode typed response for {plugin_id}.{method_name}: {error}"
                ))
            })?;
            let response = Res::decode(bytes.as_slice()).map_err(|error| {
                Status::internal(format!(
                    "failed to decode typed response for {plugin_id}.{method_name}: {error}"
                ))
            })?;
    
            let mut response = Response::new(response);
            interceptor::mark_bound_oracle_response(&mut response, bound_oracle.as_ref())?;
            Ok(response)
        }
    }

    //! Shared JSON Schema field mapping for sealing, build and runtime gRPC adapters.
    //! Contracts are supplied by PluginSchema; this module owns no declarations.
    //!
    //! Dynamic Value/Struct/ListValue numbers use protobuf's IEEE-754 doubles.
    //! Declared integer fields use int64/uint64 and retain their full range.
    use serde_json::Value;
    #[cfg(test)]
    use serde_json::json;
    
    /// Proto3 scalar presence distinguishes an omitted argument from an explicit
    /// false, zero, or empty string before validating the owning plugin schema.
    pub fn needs_scalar_presence(proto_type: &str, repeated: bool) -> bool {
        !repeated && !proto_type.starts_with("google.protobuf.")
    }
    
    pub fn json_schema_type_to_proto(schema: &Value) -> (String, bool) {
        classify(schema, 0)
    }
    
    fn classify(schema: &Value, depth: usize) -> (String, bool) {
        if depth >= 64 {
            return ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false);
        }
        if let Some(alternatives) = schema
            .get("anyOf")
            .or_else(|| schema.get("oneOf"))
            .and_then(Value::as_array)
        {
            // Value preserves null and heterogeneous unions without inventing a
            // default scalar, or discarding one branch of the plugin's contract.
            if alternatives.len() != 1 {
                return ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false);
            }
            return classify(&alternatives[0], depth + 1);
        }
        if let Some(kinds) = schema.get("type").and_then(Value::as_array) {
            if kinds.len() != 1 || kinds[0] == "null" {
                return ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false);
            }
            let mut single = schema.clone();
            single["type"] = kinds[0].clone();
            return classify(&single, depth + 1);
        }
        if let Some(values) = schema.get("enum").and_then(Value::as_array) {
            return if values.iter().all(Value::is_string) {
                ("string".into(), false)
            } else {
                ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false)
            };
        }
        match schema.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            Some("string") => ("string".into(), false),
            Some("boolean") => ("bool".into(), false),
            Some("integer") => {
                let unsigned = schema
                    .get("format")
                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
                    .is_some_and(|format| format.starts_with("uint"))
                    || schema
                        .get("minimum")
                        .and_then(Value::as_f64)
                        .is_some_and(|minimum| minimum >= 0.0);
                (if unsigned { "uint64" } else { "int64" }.into(), false)
            }
            Some("number") => ("double".into(), false),
            Some("array") => {
                let (kind, repeated) = schema
                    .get("items")
                    .map(|item| classify(item, depth + 1))
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false));
                // Protobuf has no repeated repeated scalar. Each inner array is
                // represented by ListValue so matrix boundaries survive the wire.
                (
                    if repeated {
                        "google.protobuf.ListValue".into()
                    } else {
                        kind
                    },
                    true,
                )
            }
            Some("object") => ("google.protobuf.Struct".into(), false),
            _ if schema.get("properties").is_some() => ("google.protobuf.Struct".into(), false),
            _ => ("google.protobuf.Value".into(), false),
        }
    }

    pub fn blobify_plugin_schema(
        plugin_id: &str,
        schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema,
    ) -> PluginObjectBlob {

    }
    
    /// Seal the FULL canonical workspace schema. The sealed SCHEMA_JSON section
    /// (and the schema hash) is the complete `op_state_store::PluginSchema` —
    /// signals, guarantees, category and all. The reduced local `PluginSchema` is
    /// derived from the same canonical value purely as the working view for
    /// descriptor/manifest synthesis; it is never what gets sealed.
    pub fn blobify_plugin_schema_with_identity(
        plugin_id: &str,
        mut schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema,
        identity: Option<BlobIdentity>,
    ) -> PluginObjectBlob {
        schema.name = blob::canonical_plugin_id(plugin_id);
        let canonical_value =
            serde_json::to_value(&schema).expect("op-state-store PluginSchema serializes");
        // serde_json's Map is BTreeMap-backed (no `preserve_order`), so this is
        // deterministic key-sorted canonical JSON.
        let canonical_json =
            serde_json::to_string(&canonical_value).expect("canonical value serializes");
        let working: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(canonical_value)
            .expect("op-blob PluginSchema view accepts op-state-store schema");
        blob::blobify_canonical(&working, canonical_json, identity)
    }

    //! Derive review artifacts from the plugin-owned contract; JSON is never an input.
    #[path = "../../op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched_fs_contract.rs"]
    mod threetched_fs_contract;
    
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail, ensure};
    use serde_json::json;
    
    fn exports() -> Result<Vec<(&'static str, Vec<u8>)>> {
        let contract = threetched_fs_contract::document();
        ensure!(
            contract["versioning"]["schema_version"] == threetched_fs_contract::schema_version()
                && contract["versioning"]["source_commit"] == threetched_fs_contract::source_commit(),
            "contract accessors and embedded versioning disagree"
        );
        jsonschema::draft202012::meta::validate(&contract)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid embedded JSON Schema: {error}"))?;
        let schema = threetched_fs_contract::schema_document();
        jsonschema::Validator::new(&schema)?
            .validate(&contract)
            .map_err(|error| anyhow::anyhow!("embedded contract fails its own schema: {error}"))?;
        let binding = json!({
            "authority": {
                "authoring_source": contract["authority"]["authoring_source"],
                "derivation": "Generated by typed_export from the plugin-owned document; do not edit this file."
            },
            "types": contract["types"],
            "methods": contract["methods"],
            "bindings": contract["bindings"]
        });
        [
            ("typed-filesystem.schema.json", contract.clone()),
            ("typed-filesystem-binding-input.json", binding),
            (
                "typed-filesystem-provenance.json",
                contract["versioning"].clone(),
            ),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(name, value)| {
            let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&value)?;
            bytes.push(b'\n');
            Ok((name, bytes))
        })
        .collect()
    }
    
    fn export(directory: &Path, check: bool) -> Result<()> {
        let documents = exports()?;
        if !check {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(directory)?;
        }
        for (name, bytes) in documents {
            let path = directory.join(name);
            if check {
                let current = std::fs::read(&path)
                    .with_context(|| format!("missing export {}; run typed_export", path.display()))?;
                ensure!(
                    current == bytes,
                    "stale export {}; run typed_export",
                    path.display()
                );
            } else {
                std::fs::write(&path, bytes).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<()> {
        let mut check = false;
        let mut directory = PathBuf::from("crates/threetched-fs/docs");
        let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
        while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
            match arg.as_str() {
                "--check" => check = true,
                "--out-dir" => directory = args.next().context("--out-dir requires a path")?.into(),
                _ => bail!("unknown argument {arg}; expected --check or --out-dir PATH"),
            }
        }
        export(&directory, check)?;
        println!(
            "{} plugin-owned 3tchedFS contract exports in {}",
            if check { "Verified" } else { "Wrote" },
            directory.display()
        );
        Ok(())
    }

        fn protobuf_numbers(value: &Value) -> Value {
            match value {
                Value::Number(number) => json!(number.as_f64().unwrap()),
                Value::Array(values) => Value::Array(values.iter().map(protobuf_numbers).collect()),
                Value::Object(values) => Value::Object(
                    values
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), protobuf_numbers(value)))
                        .collect(),
                ),
                other => other.clone(),
            }
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn u64_bound_is_exact_through_protobuf_schema_numbers() {
            let contract = threetched_fs_contract::document();
            let too_large: Value = serde_json::from_str("18446744073709551616").unwrap();
            for schema in [
                contract["$defs"]["U64"].clone(),
                protobuf_numbers(&contract["$defs"]["U64"]),
            ] {
                let validator = jsonschema::Validator::new(&schema).unwrap();
                assert!(validator.is_valid(&json!(u64::MAX)));
                assert!(!validator.is_valid(&too_large));
                assert!(!validator.is_valid(&json!(-1)));
            }
        }

    # Export the plugin-owned contract. The execution worker must run this helper;
    # it invokes Cargo and never assembles a schema from documentation inputs.
    set -eu
    cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."
    case "${CARGO_CALLER_FAMILY:-}" in
      gpt|grok|claude) ;;
      *) printf '%s\n' 'Set CARGO_CALLER_FAMILY to your model family and delegate this Cargo helper to the execution worker.' >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    exec cargo run --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p threetched-fs --example typed_export -- "$@"

    /// Trait used to modify a constructed schema and optionally its subschemas.

    pub trait Transform {

        ///
        /// When overriding this method, you may want to call the [`transform_subschemas`] function to
        /// also transform any subschemas.
        fn transform(&mut self, schema: &mut Schema);

            f.write_str(core::any::type_name::<Self>())
        }
    }
    
    impl<F> Transform for F
    where

    +/// Derive an order-independent exact JSON value schema from the sole authority.
    +fn literal_schema(value: &serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value {
    +    use serde_json::{Value, json};
    +    match value {
    +        Value::Object(fields) => {
    +            let properties: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = fields.iter()
    +                .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), literal_schema(value)))
    +                .collect();
    +            json!({
    +                "type": "object", "properties": properties,
    +                "required": fields.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    +                "additionalProperties": false,
    +            })
    +        }
    +        Value::Array(items) => {
    +            let mut schema = json!({
    +                "type": "array", "minItems": items.len(),
    +                "maxItems": items.len(), "items": false,
    +            });
    +            if !items.is_empty() {
    +                schema["prefixItems"] = items.iter().map(literal_schema).collect();
    +            }
    +            schema
    +        }
    +        _ => json!({"const": value}),
    +    }
    +}

    /// SCHEMA_JSON section — and therefore the schema hash — covers the complete
    /// contract, never a reduced projection of it.
    pub fn blobify_canonical(
        schema: &PluginSchema,
        schema_json: String,
        identity: Option<crate::identity::BlobIdentity>,
    ) -> PluginObjectBlob {
        let plugin_id = canonical_plugin_id(&schema.name);
        let schema_hash = {
            let mut h = Sha256::new();
            h.update(schema_json.as_bytes());
            hex(&h.finalize())
        };
    
        let (descriptor_set, method_infos) = descriptor::descriptor_set_for_plugin(&plugin_id, schema);
    
        let mut methods: Vec<MethodManifest> = method_infos
            .iter()
            .map(|d| {
                let decl = schema
                    .methods
                    .get(&d.schema_name)
                    .expect("descriptor method must come from PluginSchema.methods");
                MethodManifest {
                    schema_name: d.schema_name.clone(),
                    grpc_name: descriptor::pascal_case(&decl.name),
                    grpc_path: d.grpc_path.clone(),
                    grpc_service: d.service_full.clone(),
                    grpc_file: d.file_name.clone(),
                    input_message: d.input_full.clone(),
                    output_message: d.output_full.clone(),
                    subid: decl.subid.clone(),
                    required_capability: decl.required_capability.clone(),
                    side_effect: decl.side_effect,
                    idempotent: decl.idempotent,
                    symbols: d.symbols.clone(),
                }
            })
            .collect();
        methods.sort_by(|a, b| a.schema_name.cmp(&b.schema_name));
    
        let mut services: Vec<String> = methods.iter().map(|m| m.grpc_service.clone()).collect();
        services.sort();
        let mut files: Vec<String> = methods.iter().map(|m| m.grpc_file.clone()).collect();
        files.sort();
    
        let manifest = BlobManifest {
            blob_type: default_blob_type(),
            plugin_id: plugin_id.clone(),
            schema_version: schema.version.clone(),
            schema_hash,
            dbus: DbusIdentity {
                bus_name: "org.opdbus.v1.plugins".to_string(),
                object_path: format!("/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id}"),
                interface_name: "org.opdbus.v1.PluginV1".to_string(),
            },
            grpc: GrpcIdentity { services, files },
            identity,
            methods,
        };
    
        let meta = serde_json::json!({
            "blob_format": FORMAT_VERSION,
            "dialect": schema.dialect,
            "subids": schema.subids,
            "immutable_paths": schema.immutable_paths,
            "json_schema": schema.to_json_schema(),
        });
    
        PluginObjectBlob {
            manifest,
            schema_json,
            descriptor_set,
            meta_json: serde_json::to_string(&meta).expect("meta serializes"),
        }
    }
    
    ) -> PluginObjectBlob {
        schema.name = blob::canonical_plugin_id(plugin_id);
        let canonical_value =
            serde_json::to_value(&schema).expect("op-state-store PluginSchema serializes");
        // serde_json's Map is BTreeMap-backed (no `preserve_order`), so this is
        // deterministic key-sorted canonical JSON.
        let canonical_json =
            serde_json::to_string(&canonical_value).expect("canonical value serializes");
        let working: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(canonical_value)
            .expect("op-blob PluginSchema view accepts op-state-store schema");
        blob::blobify_canonical(&working, canonical_json, identity)
    }

    /// public disclosure policy remains the exact sealed policy; it is not inferred
    /// from compiled fields. Method admission and caller authorization are separate.
    /// This does not establish an atomic catalog/state transaction.
    pub(crate) fn admit_compiled_state_contract(
        pinned: &ManifestPinnedSchemaDocument,
        plugin_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        anyhow::ensure!(
            pinned.schema.name == plugin_id && pinned.blob.manifest.plugin_id == plugin_id,
            "pinned state contract is not for expected plugin {plugin_id}"
        );
        let compiled = compiled_contracts()?
            .get(plugin_id)
            .with_context(|| format!("no compiled state compatibility evidence for {plugin_id}"))?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            pinned.schema.version == compiled.version,
            "compiled/sealed state version mismatch for {plugin_id}: compiled {}, sealed {}; align the binary and sealed catalog before accessing typed state",
            compiled.version,
            pinned.schema.version
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            pinned.schema.fields == compiled.fields,
            "compiled/sealed state field contract mismatch for {plugin_id}; align the binary and sealed catalog before accessing typed state"
        );
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Re-read the pinned catalog and reject contract drift before backend effects.
    ///
    /// Use the canonical schema method key, not a transport alias. The returned
    /// declaration comes from the exact pinned snapshot checked here; callers can
    /// use its arguments for separately normalized input validation. This function
    /// does not admit identity, grant capability, or claim a cross-call catalog lock.
    pub(crate) fn admit_compiled_method(
        plugin_id: &str,
        canonical_method: &str,
        exercised_capability: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<MethodDecl> {
        Ok(admit_compiled_invocation(plugin_id, canonical_method, exercised_capability)?.0)
    }
    
    /// Retain the complete admitted plugin for methods which consume its catalog
    /// metadata. A second catalog read could observe a different seal.
    pub(crate) fn admit_compiled_invocation(
        plugin_id: &str,
        canonical_method: &str,
        exercised_capability: Option<&str>,
        compiled: &CompiledContracts,
    ) -> Result<MethodDecl> {
        let declaration = pinned
            .schema
            .methods
            .get(canonical_method)
            .with_context(|| {
                format!("method {plugin_id}.{canonical_method} is absent from pinned seal")
            })?;
        let compiled_plugin = compiled.get(plugin_id).with_context(|| {
            format!("no compiled method compatibility evidence for sealed plugin {plugin_id}")
        })?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            pinned.schema.version == compiled_plugin.version,
            "compiled/sealed plugin version mismatch for {plugin_id}: compiled {}, sealed {}; align the binary and sealed catalog before dispatch",
            compiled_plugin.version,
            pinned.schema.version
        );
        let compiled_method = compiled_plugin
            .methods
            .get(canonical_method)
            .with_context(|| {
                format!("no compiled method compatibility evidence for {plugin_id}.{canonical_method}")
            })?;
        anyhow::ensure!(
            declaration == compiled_method,
            "compiled/sealed method contract mismatch for {plugin_id}.{canonical_method}; align the binary and sealed catalog before dispatch"
        );
        anyhow::ensure!(
            declaration.required_capability.as_deref() == exercised_capability,
            "exercised capability differs from pinned method {plugin_id}.{canonical_method}"
        );

## User

will this have to be updated after fixes and are they easy fixes?

## Assistant

Yes. Fixes that change behavior need a contract update—especially caching, read consistency, errors, or receipts. The schema and Rust bindings are then regenerated from the plugin-owned contract.

Difficulty varies:

- **Smaller:** cache flags and metadata corrections.
- **Moderate:** removing retained caches, bounded buffers, receipt validation, and symlink handling.
- **Larger:** committed-state reads with identity isolation, workspace conflict handling, and a safe direct-SHM layout.

Most are fixable without a redesign. Direct-SHM support is the largest change and can remain unavailable until its guarantees are implemented.

    /// Kernel cache lifetime for a pinned view. Its tree never changes, and file
    /// contents stay live because every open uses direct I/O. Workspaces rebuild
    /// their tree on write, so they are never cached.
    const VIEW_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
    
    /// Identifies one committed version of a state file. MutationEngine replaces
    /// the file on every commit, so a new commit always yields a new key.
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct StateKey {
        dev: u64,
        ino: u64,
        mtime: i64,
        mtime_nsec: i64,
        len: u64,
    }
    
    /// Rendered live-file bytes by (plugin, pointer), each tagged with the state
    /// version it was rendered from.
    type LiveCache = HashMap<(String, String), (StateKey, Vec<u8>)>;
    
    impl StateKey {
        fn of(metadata: &std::fs::Metadata) -> Self {
            use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
            Self {
                dev: metadata.dev(),
                ino: metadata.ino(),
                mtime: metadata.mtime(),
                mtime_nsec: metadata.mtime_nsec(),
                len: metadata.len(),
            }
        }
    }
    
    type OperationCompletion = Option<Result<Vec<u8>, (i32, Vec<u8>)>>;
    
    struct OpenFile {
        ino: u64,
        bytes: Vec<u8>,

    }

        /// A live view for one identity, with a lungs `call` file per method.
        pub fn build_lungs(
            store: &ObjectStore,
            target: ProjectionTarget,

        ) -> Result<Self> {

        pub fn build_with(
            store: &ObjectStore,
            target: ProjectionTarget,
            state_dir: Option<&std::path::Path>,
            lungs: bool,
        ) -> Result<Self> {
            let (view, workspace) = match &target {
                ProjectionTarget::View(id) => (store.read_view(id)?, None),
                ProjectionTarget::Workspace(id) => {
                    let workspace = store.read_workspace(id)?;
                    let view = store.read_view(&workspace.base_view)?;
                    (view, Some(workspace))
                }
            };
            // View mounts read live state from SHM; workspace mounts use frozen COW.
            let live = workspace.is_none() && state_dir.is_some();
            let mut builder =
                NamespaceBuilder::new(target.clone(), state_dir.map(|p| p.to_path_buf()), lungs);
            builder.add_root_metadata(&view, workspace.as_ref())?;
    
            let plugins = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "plugins")?;
            let operations = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "operations")?;
            let relationships = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "relationships")?;
            let dependencies = builder.add_dir(relationships, "dependencies")?;
            let capabilities = builder.add_dir(ROOT_INO, "capabilities")?;
    
            for plugin_id in view.objects.keys() {
                let object = match &workspace {
                    Some(workspace) => store.workspace_object(workspace, plugin_id)?,
                    None => store.object_for_view(&view, plugin_id)?,
                };
                let plugin_name = encode_component(plugin_id);
                let plugin_dir = builder.add_dir(plugins, &plugin_name)?;
                builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "object.blob.json", &object, None)?;
                builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "schema.json", &object.schema, None)?;
                if live {
                    builder.add_live_file(plugin_dir, "value.json", plugin_id, "")?;
                } else {
                    builder.add_json(plugin_dir, "value.json", &object.value, None)?;
                }
                builder.add_json(
                    plugin_dir,
                    "capabilities.json",
                    &object.schema.required_capabilities(),
                    None,
                )?;
                builder.add_text(
                    plugin_dir,
                    "object.hash",
                    format!(
                        "{}\n",
                        object_hash_for_target(&view, workspace.as_ref(), plugin_id)?
                    )
                    .into_bytes(),
                    None,
                )?;
    
                let data_dir = builder.add_dir(plugin_dir, "data")?;
                let workspace_id = workspace
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|workspace| workspace.workspace_id.clone());
                builder.add_value_children(
                    data_dir,
                    plugin_id,
                    "",
                    &object.value,
                    Some(&object.schema),
                    None,
                    workspace_id.as_deref(),
                    !object.schema.tags.iter().any(|tag| tag == "immutable"),
                    live,
                )?;
    
                let methods_dir = builder.add_dir(plugin_dir, "operations")?;
                let root_methods_dir = builder.add_dir(operations, &plugin_name)?;
                for (method_name, method) in &object.schema.methods {
                    let encoded = encode_component(method_name);
                    let method_dir = builder.add_dir(methods_dir, &encoded)?;
                    builder.add_json(method_dir, "input.schema.json", &method.args, None)?;
                    if let Some(returns) = &method.returns {
                        builder.add_json(method_dir, "output.schema.json", returns, None)?;
                    }
                    builder.add_json(method_dir, "metadata.json", method, None)?;
                    if lungs {
                        builder.add_lungs_files(method_dir, plugin_id, method_name)?;
                    }
                    builder.add_symlink(
                        root_methods_dir,
                        &encoded,
                        format!("/plugins/{plugin_name}/operations/{encoded}"),
                    )?;
    
                    if let Some(capability) = &method.required_capability {
                        let capability_dir =
                            builder.add_dir_idempotent(capabilities, &encode_component(capability))?;
                        builder.add_symlink(
                            capability_dir,
                            &format!("{plugin_name}.{}", encode_component(method_name)),
                            format!("/plugins/{plugin_name}/operations/{encoded}"),
                        )?;
                    }
                }
    
                let relation_dir = builder.add_dir(dependencies, &plugin_name)?;
                for dependency in &object.schema.dependencies {
                    builder.add_symlink(
                        relation_dir,
                        &encode_component(dependency),
                        format!("/plugins/{}", encode_component(dependency)),
                    )?;
                }
            }
    
            Ok(builder.finish())
        }
    
        pub fn node(&self, ino: u64) -> Option<&Node> {
            self.nodes.get(&ino)
        }
    
        pub fn lookup(&self, parent: u64, name: &std::ffi::OsStr) -> Option<&Node> {
            let ino = self.children.get(&parent)?.get(name)?;
            self.nodes.get(ino)
        }
    
        pub fn children(&self, parent: u64) -> Option<&BTreeMap<OsString, u64>> {
            self.children.get(&parent)
        }
    
        /// Public mount declaration, never a credential or inferred identity.
        /// The caller supplies only the socket mount's declared session selector.
        pub(crate) fn declare_socket_session(&mut self, session: &str) -> Result<()> {
            let node = self
                .lookup(ROOT_INO, std::ffi::OsStr::new(".3tchedfs.json"))
                .context("mount metadata missing")?;
            let NodeKind::File(bytes) = &node.kind else {
                bail!("mount metadata is not a file")
            };
            let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes.read())?;
            value["session_id"] = Value::String(session.to_owned());
            let mut rendered = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&value)?;
            rendered.push(b'\n');
            *bytes.write() = rendered;
            Ok(())
        }
    }

                    source_catalog_hash: &view.source_catalog_hash,
                    source_catalog_generation: view.source_catalog_generation,
                    object_count: view.objects.len(),
                    invocation: view
                        .objects
